sources.title: Interest in Trump’s meme coin dinner fades as $TRUMP sinks to record lows - Yahoo Finance
passages: Today, interest in the third meme coin dinner ​contest has collapsed.
It invited 185 holders of the token, known as $TRUMP, to register and see who held the largest amounts during the contest scoring period from September 30 to November 16.
The leaderboard at closing showed only 130 crypto wallets — holding a combined $8.6 million — a 94% drop from the first dinner.
The contest's muted results come at a time when the Trump family's other crypto-connected equities and ventures have also deflated to record lows.
Together, outside investors in ​the ​five main crypto and crypto-linked projects have lost more than $5 billion, according to Reuters estimates.

NEW YORK, Nov 16 (Reuters) - As winners were being determined on Monday for President Donald Trump's third crypto gala dinner, scheduled for November 22 at his golf club outside Washington, the president's meme coin was trading near 92 cents, a bruising tumble from its high ‌in 2025 of more than $74.
In total, a Reuters analysis found that the Trumps have earned at least $2.3 billion through ​April from their four main crypto ventures, including the meme coin.

Wealthy ‌crypto investors collectively wagered $148 million on what the president promoted as the "most EXCLUSIVE INVITATION in the world." The holdings needed to win a seat at the dinner ranged from $59,000 to $18.5 million.
The Trump meme coin project and the Trump Organization did not respond to a request for comment.
He ⁠came in at 26th on the leaderboard with about $41,000 in time-weighted Trump token holdings.
His 23-year-old sister, Gabrielle Felen, is also coming along.
She was disappointed she did not make the top 120 — now, she will not get the gift bag.
Most of those losses ​came before the midterm elections in which the Democrats dealt a heavy ‌defeat to Trump's Republican Party, a result that sent prices even lower.

extraction.body: NEW YORK, Nov 16 (Reuters) - As winners were being determined on Monday for President Donald Trump's third crypto gala dinner, scheduled for November 22 at his golf club outside Washington, the president's meme coin was trading near 92 cents, a bruising tumble from its high ‌in 2025 of more than $74. At the peak of Trump's popularity, the token's price surged more than 60% when the first contest was announced in April 2025. Wealthy ‌crypto investors collectively wagered $148 million on what the president promoted as the "most EXCLUSIVE INVITATION in the world." The holdings needed to win a seat at the dinner ranged from $59,000 to $18.5 million. Today, interest in the third meme coin dinner ​contest has collapsed. It invited 185 holders of the token, known as $TRUMP, to register and see who held the largest amounts during the contest scoring period from September 30 to November 16. The leaderboard at closing showed only 130 crypto wallets — holding a combined $8.6 million — a 94% drop from the first dinner. The top 29 wallets will be awarded a "Special VIP Reception" with "YOUR FAVORITE PRESIDENT," according to the contest's website, along with VIP seating at the dinner. This will be the third time Morten Christensen, a crypto entrepreneur from the Netherlands, has qualified for the dinner, but the first where ‌he will be at the VIP reception with the president. He ⁠came in at 26th on the leaderboard with about $41,000 in time-weighted Trump token holdings. "You can be in a room with the president of the United States, arguably one of the most powerful people in the world," said Christensen. "So why would I not go if it cost me ⁠almost nothing to go?" His 23-year-old sister, Gabrielle Felen, is also coming along. She bought about 2,000 Trump tokens. She was disappointed she did not make the top 120 — now, she will not get the gift bag. The contest's muted results come at a time when the Trump family's other crypto-connected equities and ventures have also deflated to record lows. Together, outside investors in ​the ​five main crypto and crypto-linked projects have lost more than $5 billion, according to Reuters estimates. Most of those losses ​came before the midterm elections in which the Democrats dealt a heavy ‌defeat to Trump's Republican Party, a result that sent prices even lower. Because the price of the Trump token has continued to fall sharply during the holding period in the run-up to the dinner, the winners have lost millions of dollars in recent weeks. The Trump meme coin project and the Trump Organization did not respond to a request for comment. The White House also did not respond to a request for comment but has repeatedly said there is no conflict of interest because the president's assets are in a trust run by his children. While most buyers have been left with losses, the Trump meme coin has so far earned the Trump family at least $635 million, according to the president's June ‌financial disclosure statement. In total, a Reuters analysis found that the Trumps have earned at least $2.3 billion through ​April from their four main crypto ventures, including the meme coin. The president's stake in the fifth crypto-linked ​venture, Trump Media & Technology Group, is worth about $500 million. The billions the Trump family ​has earned while in office have drawn opposition from congressional Democrats, who retook control of both the US Senate and US House of Representatives in the midterm ‌elections. They will now have subpoena power and the ability to ​launch investigations and conduct hearings about what US ​Senator Elizabeth Warren, a Massachusetts Democrat who will lead oversight on the Senate Banking Committee, has characterized as "an orgy of corruption." Warren said last Monday that the Trump family crypto businesses will be a focus of her accountability investigations. Crypto wallets are anonymous and known only by strings of letters and numbers. The anonymity is what ​prompted government ethics officials to raise concern about the first two ‌dinners because they said the meme coin could be a conduit for anonymous foreign individuals looking to purchase access to the president. Blockchain analysis showed that ​of the 220 wallets that competed in the first contest, more than half were likely based outside the United States. (Reporting by Michelle Conlin in New ​York and Tom Bergin in London; Editing by Tom Lasseter, Matthew Lewis and Nick Zieminski)

At the peak of Trump's popularity, the token's price surged more than 60% when the first contest was announced in April 2025. Wealthy ‌crypto investors collectively wagered $148 million on what the president promoted as the "most EXCLUSIVE INVITATION in the world." The holdings needed to win a seat at the dinner ranged from $59,000 to $18.5 million.

Today, interest in the third meme coin dinner ​contest has collapsed. It invited 185 holders of the token, known as $TRUMP, to register and see who held the largest amounts during the contest scoring period from September 30 to November 16. The leaderboard at closing showed only 130 crypto wallets — holding a combined $8.6 million — a 94% drop from the first dinner.
The top 29 wallets will be awarded a "Special VIP Reception" with "YOUR FAVORITE PRESIDENT," according to the contest's website, along with VIP seating at the dinner.

This will be the third time Morten Christensen, a crypto entrepreneur from the Netherlands, has qualified for the dinner, but the first where ‌he will be at the VIP reception with the president. He ⁠came in at 26th on the leaderboard with about $41,000 in time-weighted Trump token holdings.
"You can be in a room with the president of the United States, arguably one of the most powerful people in the world," said Christensen. "So why would I not go if it cost me ⁠almost nothing to go?"
His 23-year-old sister, Gabrielle Felen, is also coming along. She bought about 2,000 Trump tokens. She was disappointed she did not make the top 120 — now, she will not get the gift bag.

The contest's muted results come at a time when the Trump family's other crypto-connected equities and ventures have also deflated to record lows. Together, outside investors in ​the ​five main crypto and crypto-linked projects have lost more than $5 billion, according to Reuters estimates.
Most of those losses ​came before the midterm elections in which the Democrats dealt a heavy ‌defeat to Trump's Republican Party, a result that sent prices even lower.
Because the price of the Trump token has continued to fall sharply during the holding period in the run-up to the dinner, the winners have lost millions of dollars in recent weeks.

The Trump meme coin project and the Trump Organization did not respond to a request for comment. The White House also did not respond to a request for comment but has repeatedly said there is no conflict of interest because the president's assets are in a trust run by his children.

While most buyers have been left with losses, the Trump meme coin has so far earned the Trump family at least $635 million, according to the president's June ‌financial disclosure statement. In total, a Reuters analysis found that the Trumps have earned at least $2.3 billion through ​April from their four main crypto ventures, including the meme coin. The president's stake in the fifth crypto-linked ​venture, Trump Media & Technology Group, is worth about $500 million.

The billions the Trump family ​has earned while in office have drawn opposition from congressional Democrats, who retook control of both the US Senate and US House of Representatives in the midterm ‌elections. They will now have subpoena power and the ability to ​launch investigations and conduct hearings about what US ​Senator Elizabeth Warren, a Massachusetts Democrat who will lead oversight on the Senate Banking Committee, has characterized as "an orgy of corruption." Warren said last Monday that the Trump family crypto businesses will be a focus of her accountability investigations.

Crypto wallets are anonymous and known only by strings of letters and numbers. The anonymity is what ​prompted government ethics officials to raise concern about the first two ‌dinners because they said the meme coin could be a conduit for anonymous foreign individuals looking to purchase access to the president. Blockchain analysis showed that ​of the 220 wallets that competed in the first contest, more than half were likely based outside the United States.
(Reporting by Michelle Conlin in New ​York and Tom Bergin in London; Editing by Tom Lasseter, Matthew Lewis and Nick Zieminski)

passages: The president presided over an upscale dinner for investors in his collapsing meme coin, celebrating the venture even as the price of admission has plummeted.
A pump-up dancer in a Trump mask greeted them.

VIP guests received gold-tone Trump diver watches and Trump-branded “Victory” fragrances at his Northern Virginia golf club, where they rubbed shoulders with retired athletes Floyd Mayweather and Tristan Thompson.
Mentalist Lior Suchard claimed to read their minds.
In a reception room here where chandeliers abounded and women less so, top collectors of President Donald Trump’s novelty crypto token gathered to graze on fall harvest salad and filet mignon.

sources.title: Trump’s Meme Coin Dinner Is Back Tonight: But This Time Almost Nobody Wants a Seat - CryptoPotato
passages: CryptoPotato reported that Trump’s first dinner in May 2025 was limited to the top 220 holders, with the leading 25 receiving an additional reception and VIP experiences.
The announcement initially sent the token flying, even after it had crumbled at the time.
Reports and Wu Blockchain noted that the POTUS will host the dinner for top TRUMP holders even as the number of participants has declined sharply.

Crypto Trader Morten Christensen told Bloomberg that hedging his holdings reduced his effective cost of qualifying from roughly $1,200 for the first dinner and $500 for the second to an approximately $6 profit this time.
Coin Bureau highlighted an even more striking comparison, with one participant reportedly securing a place after buying only $518 worth of the meme coin.
Reuters reported that only 130 wallets made the final leaderboard this time, collectively holding $8.6 million worth of TRUMP.
The newest event has at least 5,000 wallets eligible to participate but never registered, even after organizers extended the deadline by four days.
This significant decline in demand has mimicked the underlying asset’s performance to a large extent.
TRUMP currently trades well below $1 after peaking at $74-$75 shortly following its January 2025 launch.
This means that the asset has lost almost 99% of its value in less than two years.
The second gala announced for April 2026 produced a similar immediate reaction.
TRUMP surged more than 50% from its then-ATL after organizers invited the top 297 holders to an event at Mar-a-Lago, with 29 qualifying for a VIP reception.
According to some reports, participants have qualified for just $518 now, while thousands of eligible wallets never even registered, as TRUMP continues to lose value.

extraction.body: NEW YORK, Nov 16 (Reuters) - As winners were being determined on Monday for President Donald Trump's third crypto gala dinner, scheduled for November 22 at his golf club outside Washington, the president's meme coin was trading near 92 cents, a bruising tumble from its high ‌in 2025 of more than $74. At the peak of Trump's popularity, the token's price surged more than 60% when the first contest was announced in April 2025. Wealthy ‌crypto investors collectively wagered $148 million on what the president promoted as the "most EXCLUSIVE INVITATION in the world." The holdings needed to win a seat at the dinner ranged from $59,000 to $18.5 million. Today, interest in the third meme coin dinner ​contest has collapsed. It invited 185 holders of the token, known as $TRUMP, to register and see who held the largest amounts during the contest scoring period from September 30 to November 16. The leaderboard at closing showed only 130 crypto wallets — holding a combined $8.6 million — a 94% drop from the first dinner. The top 29 wallets will be awarded a "Special VIP Reception" with "YOUR FAVORITE PRESIDENT," according to the contest's website, along with VIP seating at the dinner. This will be the third time Morten Christensen, a crypto entrepreneur from the Netherlands, has qualified for the dinner, but the first where ‌he will be at the VIP reception with the president. He ⁠came in at 26th on the leaderboard with about $41,000 in time-weighted Trump token holdings. "You can be in a room with the president of the United States, arguably one of the most powerful people in the world," said Christensen. "So why would I not go if it cost me ⁠almost nothing to go?" His 23-year-old sister, Gabrielle Felen, is also coming along. She bought about 2,000 Trump tokens. She was disappointed she did not make the top 120 — now, she will not get the gift bag. The contest's muted results come at a time when the Trump family's other crypto-connected equities and ventures have also deflated to record lows. Together, outside investors in ​the ​five main crypto and crypto-linked projects have lost more than $5 billion, according to Reuters estimates. Most of those losses ​came before the midterm elections in which the Democrats dealt a heavy ‌defeat to Trump's Republican Party, a result that sent prices even lower. Because the price of the Trump token has continued to fall sharply during the holding period in the run-up to the dinner, the winners have lost millions of dollars in recent weeks. The Trump meme coin project and the Trump Organization did not respond to a request for comment. The White House also did not respond to a request for comment but has repeatedly said there is no conflict of interest because the president's assets are in a trust run by his children. While most buyers have been left with losses, the Trump meme coin has so far earned the Trump family at least $635 million, according to the president's June ‌financial disclosure statement. In total, a Reuters analysis found that the Trumps have earned at least $2.3 billion through ​April from their four main crypto ventures, including the meme coin. The president's stake in the fifth crypto-linked ​venture, Trump Media & Technology Group, is worth about $500 million. The billions the Trump family ​has earned while in office have drawn opposition from congressional Democrats, who retook control of both the US Senate and US House of Representatives in the midterm ‌elections. They will now have subpoena power and the ability to ​launch investigations and conduct hearings about what US ​Senator Elizabeth Warren, a Massachusetts Democrat who will lead oversight on the Senate Banking Committee, has characterized as "an orgy of corruption." Warren said last Monday that the Trump family crypto businesses will be a focus of her accountability investigations. Crypto wallets are anonymous and known only by strings of letters and numbers. The anonymity is what ​prompted government ethics officials to raise concern about the first two ‌dinners because they said the meme coin could be a conduit for anonymous foreign individuals looking to purchase access to the president. Blockchain analysis showed that ​of the 220 wallets that competed in the first contest, more than half were likely based outside the United States. (Reporting by Michelle Conlin in New ​York and Tom Bergin in London; Editing by Tom Lasseter, Matthew Lewis and Nick Zieminski)

The billions the Trump family ​has earned while in office have drawn opposition from congressional Democrats, who retook control of both the US Senate and US House of Representatives in the midterm ‌elections. They will now have subpoena power and the ability to ​launch investigations and conduct hearings about what US ​Senator Elizabeth Warren, a Massachusetts Democrat who will lead oversight on the Senate Banking Committee, has characterized as "an orgy of corruption." Warren said last Monday that the Trump family crypto businesses will be a focus of her accountability investigations.

Crypto wallets are anonymous and known only by strings of letters and numbers. The anonymity is what ​prompted government ethics officials to raise concern about the first two ‌dinners because they said the meme coin could be a conduit for anonymous foreign individuals looking to purchase access to the president. Blockchain analysis showed that ​of the 220 wallets that competed in the first contest, more than half were likely based outside the United States.

sources.title: Trump’s Meme Coin Dinner Is Back Tonight: But This Time Almost Nobody Wants a Seat - CryptoPotato
passages: CryptoPotato reported that Trump’s first dinner in May 2025 was limited to the top 220 holders, with the leading 25 receiving an additional reception and VIP experiences.
The announcement initially sent the token flying, even after it had crumbled at the time.
Reports and Wu Blockchain noted that the POTUS will host the dinner for top TRUMP holders even as the number of participants has declined sharply.

Crypto Trader Morten Christensen told Bloomberg that hedging his holdings reduced his effective cost of qualifying from roughly $1,200 for the first dinner and $500 for the second to an approximately $6 profit this time.
Coin Bureau highlighted an even more striking comparison, with one participant reportedly securing a place after buying only $518 worth of the meme coin.
Reuters reported that only 130 wallets made the final leaderboard this time, collectively holding $8.6 million worth of TRUMP.
The newest event has at least 5,000 wallets eligible to participate but never registered, even after organizers extended the deadline by four days.
This significant decline in demand has mimicked the underlying asset’s performance to a large extent.
TRUMP currently trades well below $1 after peaking at $74-$75 shortly following its January 2025 launch.
This means that the asset has lost almost 99% of its value in less than two years.
The second gala announced for April 2026 produced a similar immediate reaction.
TRUMP surged more than 50% from its then-ATL after organizers invited the top 297 holders to an event at Mar-a-Lago, with 29 qualifying for a VIP reception.
According to some reports, participants have qualified for just $518 now, while thousands of eligible wallets never even registered, as TRUMP continues to lose value.

passages: Berkshire Hathaway's equity portfolio has quietly become a wager on artificial intelligence, even though its most famous investor spent decades avoiding the hottest technology trends.

Three of the conglomerate's largest holdings - Apple, Coca-Cola and Alphabet - now account for 41.6% of a stock book valued at roughly $358 billion, and each is using AI to sharpen an established business rather than betting the company on it.
The company's pitch to investors is distribution: with more than 2.5 billion active devices in use worldwide, it can push AI features to consumers at a scale few rivals can match.
Its Apple Intelligence suite includes writing tools that draft and summarize messages, notification sorting and an upgraded Safari browser that can flag changes to web pages a user is tracking.
Berkshire spent about $38 billion building the stake between 2016 and 2023, and it was worth more than $170 billion by early 2024.
Because it had grown to more than half the portfolio, Buffett's team sold 75% of the position by the end of 2025 to bank gains and cut concentration risk.
Berkshire paid about $1.3 billion for 400 million shares between 1988 and 1994 and has never sold one; the stake is worth $39.5 billion and will generate $848 million in dividends this year.

The beverage maker has leaned on technology to manage a portfolio of roughly 200 brands across more than 200 countries, and in 2024 it agreed to spend $1.1 billion over five years on Microsoft's Azure cloud platform, giving it access to tools including the Copilot assistant.
Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode features are generating answers above traditional search results, which the company says is lifting search usage and pushing advertising revenue to records.
Google Cloud, meanwhile, grew revenue 103% in the quarter ended Sept.
30 and carries a $561 billion order backlog from customers waiting for more data-center capacity.
The three positions were assembled under his watch, but it is his successor, Greg Abel, who has been adding to them.
Abel took over as chief executive at the start of the year, and his most aggressive move has been in Alphabet, where Berkshire's stake has grown roughly sixfold.
Abel's buying has been concentrated in that last name.
According to The Motley Fool, he deployed an estimated $28 billion into Alphabet in the first half of 2026, including a $10 billion private placement priced at $355 a share.
He then paused in the third quarter, even as the stock traded around $340 and later fell to about $280 - below what Berkshire had paid.
The shares now change hands at roughly 21 times forward earnings.
Alphabet's weighting, while smaller, has become large enough that adding further may raise the bar for Abel, since each purchase increases portfolio concentration.
The pause last quarter suggests that calculus is already part of his thinking.
For Berkshire shareholders, the practical question is whether these three businesses can keep compounding without the companies having to win the AI race outright.
Whether that approach produces the returns that made Berkshire a $1 trillion company will now be Abel's test to meet.

Warren Buffett served as the chief executive officer of the Berkshire Hathaway ( BRKA -0.47% ) ( BRKB -0.36% ) holding company from 1965 to 2025. By the time he retired, he had turned it into a $1 trillion conglomerate with numerous wholly owned subsidiaries, a $350 billion stock portfolio, and over $300 billion in cash.

Had an investor parked $500 in Berkshire stock in 1965 and held on until Buffett stepped down, it would have grown into a whopping $24 million. The same investment in an S&P 500 ( ^GSPC -3.70% ) index fund would have grown into just $199,851 over the same period.

Buffett achieved those returns by focusing on companies with steady growth, reliable profits, and experienced management teams. He never chased the hottest trends, so you wouldn't find him piling money into artificial intelligence (AI) stocks. However, three of Berkshire's top holdings are using AI to supercharge their legacy businesses, and they represent 41.6% of the value of the conglomerate's stock portfolio.
Berkshire's new CEO, Greg Abel, has significantly increased the conglomerate's position in one of them this year. Here they are.
Warren Buffett. Image source: The Motley Fool.

Alphabet ( GOOG -2.59% ) ( GOOGL -2.70% ) is the parent company of Google, YouTube, Waymo, and a host of other subsidiaries. It has become a leader in the AI race by integrating it into legacy platforms like Google Search, and by helping businesses tap into the technology via Google Cloud.

In Google Search, the AI Overviews feature creates AI-generated responses to users' queries and places them above the traditional search results, complete with links to the relevant sources. If users wish to expand on their original query, they can open AI Mode and enter further questions into the chatbot-style interface. Alphabet says these features are fueling increased Google Search usage, driving the platform's advertising revenue to all-time highs in recent quarters.

Google Cloud, on the other hand, provides enterprises with access to computing capacity, ready-made foundation models, and other tools to help them create and deploy AI software. Its revenue surged by 103% during the recent third quarter (ended Sept. 30), but growth could accelerate even further given the platform's $561 billion order backlog from customers who are waiting for more data centers to come online.

Berkshire initially bought Alphabet stock in the third quarter of 2025, while Buffett was still at the helm, but Abel has increased the position sixfold this year. Berkshire now owns 78.8 million Class A shares and 27.2 million Class C shares worth a combined $29.6 billion.

Coca-Cola ( KO +0.94% ) is the world's largest beverage company, but building a portfolio of 200 brands and managing supply chains across more than 200 countries wouldn't be possible without the help of technology. The company has invested heavily in AI over the last few years, using it to run marketing campaigns, improve manufacturing processes, and even create new drinks.

In 2024, Coca-Cola signed a deal to spend $1.1 billion on the Microsoft ( MSFT -2.77% ) Azure cloud platform over five years, where it will access tools like the Copilot virtual assistant to support its AI transformation.

Coca-Cola is one of Berkshire's oldest holdings. Buffett spent approximately $1.3 billion acquiring 400 million shares between 1988 and 1994, and the conglomerate still holds every single one. The position is worth $39.5 billion today, and it will pay Berkshire $848 million in dividends this year alone.

Apple ( AAPL -1.90% ) is gunning to become the world's biggest distributor of AI to consumers. It boasts an installed base of more than 2.5 billion active devices around the globe, which mostly include iPhones, iPads, and Mac computers, and it's fitting them with increasingly powerful chips to run the Apple Intelligence suite of AI features and applications.

Apple Intelligence includes writing tools that can summarize and draft emails or text messages for the user. It can also prioritize notifications based on what each user deems most important. It even features an upgraded version of the Safari internet browser, which can alert the user to changes to their favorite web pages, so they know immediately if a product they were following is back in stock or is on sale.

Apple remains one of the most successful investments of Buffett's entire career. He spent approximately $38 billion accumulating shares between 2016 and 2023, and by the beginning of 2024, the position was worth over $170 billion. But it accounted for more than half the value of Berkshire's entire portfolio at that point, so Buffett and his team offloaded 75% of the conglomerate's stake by the end of 2025 to lock in gains and reduce concentration risk.
Nevertheless, it remains Berkshire's single largest position with a portfolio weighting of 22.4%, so the conglomerate will still do exceptionally well if Apple dominates the consumer AI market.

passages: Berkshire Hathaway's equity portfolio has quietly become a wager on artificial intelligence, even though its most famous investor spent decades avoiding the hottest technology trends.

Three of the conglomerate's largest holdings - Apple, Coca-Cola and Alphabet - now account for 41.6% of a stock book valued at roughly $358 billion, and each is using AI to sharpen an established business rather than betting the company on it.
The company's pitch to investors is distribution: with more than 2.5 billion active devices in use worldwide, it can push AI features to consumers at a scale few rivals can match.
Its Apple Intelligence suite includes writing tools that draft and summarize messages, notification sorting and an upgraded Safari browser that can flag changes to web pages a user is tracking.
Berkshire spent about $38 billion building the stake between 2016 and 2023, and it was worth more than $170 billion by early 2024.
Because it had grown to more than half the portfolio, Buffett's team sold 75% of the position by the end of 2025 to bank gains and cut concentration risk.
Berkshire paid about $1.3 billion for 400 million shares between 1988 and 1994 and has never sold one; the stake is worth $39.5 billion and will generate $848 million in dividends this year.

The beverage maker has leaned on technology to manage a portfolio of roughly 200 brands across more than 200 countries, and in 2024 it agreed to spend $1.1 billion over five years on Microsoft's Azure cloud platform, giving it access to tools including the Copilot assistant.
Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode features are generating answers above traditional search results, which the company says is lifting search usage and pushing advertising revenue to records.
Google Cloud, meanwhile, grew revenue 103% in the quarter ended Sept.
30 and carries a $561 billion order backlog from customers waiting for more data-center capacity.
The three positions were assembled under his watch, but it is his successor, Greg Abel, who has been adding to them.
Abel took over as chief executive at the start of the year, and his most aggressive move has been in Alphabet, where Berkshire's stake has grown roughly sixfold.
Abel's buying has been concentrated in that last name.
According to The Motley Fool, he deployed an estimated $28 billion into Alphabet in the first half of 2026, including a $10 billion private placement priced at $355 a share.
He then paused in the third quarter, even as the stock traded around $340 and later fell to about $280 - below what Berkshire had paid.
The shares now change hands at roughly 21 times forward earnings.
Alphabet's weighting, while smaller, has become large enough that adding further may raise the bar for Abel, since each purchase increases portfolio concentration.
The pause last quarter suggests that calculus is already part of his thinking.
For Berkshire shareholders, the practical question is whether these three businesses can keep compounding without the companies having to win the AI race outright.
Whether that approach produces the returns that made Berkshire a $1 trillion company will now be Abel's test to meet.

AP-Yonhap WASHINGTON — Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Friday he was frustrated with the Commerce Department’s delay in implementing restrictions over the export of certain Nvidia chips to China. Bessent said on CNBC that his department, along with the departments of State and Defense and the U.S. Trade Representative, were in favor of adding Megaspeed to an export control list for months but that the Commerce Department was in charge of the matter. “I am frustrated when President Trump made it very clear China should not receive any Nvidia chips above H100s,” he said, referring to an older generation of the company's advanced AI chips. Commerce “has the pen, and you will have to ask them about their internal processes.” Bessent's comments were an unusually public rebuke of the Commerce Department, which oversees U.S. government controls over exports of sensitive, high-tech goods. The comments come as Nvidia’s ties to Singapore-based Megaspeed International, which prominently touts the companies’ partnership on its website, play a prominent role in the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Huang allegedly had an affair with the CEO of Megaspeed, Alice Huang, who U.S. intelligence suspects is a Chinese spy, the New York Times has reported. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has come under increasing scrutiny because of his reportedly close relationship with Huang. The Times reported Thursday that Lutnick resisted placing greater limits on the sale of Nvidia's more advanced chips to China. Chinese firms have accessed Nvidia's chips through companies like Megaspeed, which has purchased more than $4 billion worth of Nvidia's advanced semiconductors. The split in President Donald Trump's cabinet reflects the widespread fallout from the scandal that has engulfed Nvidia, one of the most valuable publicly-traded companies in the world. Nvidia's computer chips play a central role in the buildout of artificial intelligence, powering AI models such as those developed by Open AI and Anthropic. The U.S. government has, since the Biden administration, sought to restrict the sale of the most advanced AI computer chips to China in an effort to protect U.S. technology companies' lead. Yet China has at times retaliated, creating controversy over how far the U.S. should push its restrictions. The Commerce Department did not immediately respond to messages seeking comment. Bessent declined to comment Friday on the Times report that he confronted Lutnick last week in the White House's situation room. Separately, Axios reported this week that Lutnick received a classified memo this spring warning about Jensen Huang's relationship with a suspected spy. Numerous members of Congress have said they will investigate Lutnick's actions and called for him to testify on Capitol Hill. Richard Neal, both Democrats, wrote Lutnick a letter demanding that he preserve all records related to decisions about Nvidia chip exports, pending an investigation. Trump's approval of advanced Nvidia chip exports to China “raises critical questions about whether and to what extent political considerations are improperly influencing policy decisions made by the Administration,” Wyden and Neal wrote. John Kennedy of Louisiana, a member of the Senate Banking Committee, said he has questions for the commerce secretary and urged him to hold a press conference to explain what he knew. “The Commerce Department greenlit $4 billion of sales of advanced chips to the company of the spy that Mr. Huang was having an affair with and I want to know why," Kennedy said. "I want to know why the Commerce Department did it in light of the export controls, and everything I read indicates that this was a decision by the secretary himself." Kennedy added that Lutnick should testify before the Senate and should be subpoenaed if necessary. Huang resigned Thursday after news that he had an affair with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who U.S. intelligence suspects to be a Chinese spy, according to The Times. Last year, Megaspeed was accused of illicitly shipping advanced Nvidia computer chips into China, but in December said there was “no evidence” of such exports. On Thursday, Megaspeed maintained it takes its obligation to comply with American export control laws “extremely seriously” — and that it was committed to working “constructively and transparently” with the U.S. government.

Trump on Friday told reporters he has “not lost confidence” in Lutnick. Lutnick is expected to testify soon before the Senate Banking Committee. Kennedy is a member of the committee. Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as the company’s CEO after he admitted to an affair with a woman suspected by U.S. officials of working with Chinese intelligence. Kennedy told NBC News that he’s less interested in talking about Huang’s affair than in examining why China was allowed to have access to the chips. “He did what he did,” the senator said of Huang. “I hope he had a good time. It was the most expensive sex since Helen of Troy.” Video of Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian working in a dimly lit, unheated office and encouraging his citizens to do the same, apparently intended as a conservation message, has drawn renewed attention to the nation’s energy crisis amid economic pressure by the United States. At one point, the president pulls up a thermostat to show that the room he’s working in is a brisk 65 degrees. An official from Iran’s Foreign Ministry told The Washington Post that these were not Pezeshkian’s real working conditions but a message about the need to save energy. “The President undertook this symbolic gesture to promote a culture of responsible energy consumption among the public,” the official said, speaking on the condition of anonymity in accordance with ministry protocol. Windows 11 offers a remarkable degree of control over how a touchpad will work, and these controls actually work the same across laptops from different manufacturers. To adjust them, open the Settings app, choose “Bluetooth & devices” and then “Touchpad.” (That should have a small label at the top saying “Your device has a precision touchpad.” If it doesn’t, your laptop is either very old or otherwise unusual.) The most important settings there reside under a “Taps” heading. “Touchpad sensitivity” adjusts when the touchpad reads a tap as the equivalent of a mouse-click; uncheck “Tap with a single finger to single-click” to have the touchpad only respond when you physically push down on it. Adjusting “Right-click zone size,” meanwhile, can cut down on the times you unintentionally right-click. AP-Yonhap WASHINGTON — Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Friday he was frustrated with the Commerce Department’s delay in implementing restrictions over the export of certain Nvidia chips to China. Bessent said on CNBC that his department, along with the departments of State and Defense and the U.S. Trade Representative, were in favor of adding Megaspeed to an export control list for months but that the Commerce Department was in charge of the matter. “I am frustrated when President Trump made it very clear China should not receive any Nvidia chips above H100s,” he said, referring to an older generation of the company's advanced AI chips. Commerce “has the pen, and you will have to ask them about their internal processes.” Bessent's comments were an unusually public rebuke of the Commerce Department, which oversees U.S. government controls over exports of sensitive, high-tech goods. The comments come as Nvidia’s ties to Singapore-based Megaspeed International, which prominently touts the companies’ partnership on its website, play a prominent role in the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Huang allegedly had an affair with the CEO of Megaspeed, Alice Huang, who U.S. intelligence suspects is a Chinese spy, the New York Times has reported. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has come under increasing scrutiny because of his reportedly close relationship with Huang. The Times reported Thursday that Lutnick resisted placing greater limits on the sale of Nvidia's more advanced chips to China. Chinese firms have accessed Nvidia's chips through companies like Megaspeed, which has purchased more than $4 billion worth of Nvidia's advanced semiconductors. The split in President Donald Trump's cabinet reflects the widespread fallout from the scandal that has engulfed Nvidia, one of the most valuable publicly-traded companies in the world. Nvidia's computer chips play a central role in the buildout of artificial intelligence, powering AI models such as those developed by Open AI and Anthropic. The U.S. government has, since the Biden administration, sought to restrict the sale of the most advanced AI computer chips to China in an effort to protect U.S. technology companies' lead. Yet China has at times retaliated, creating controversy over how far the U.S. should push its restrictions. The Commerce Department did not immediately respond to messages seeking comment. Bessent declined to comment Friday on the Times report that he confronted Lutnick last week in the White House's situation room. Separately, Axios reported this week that Lutnick received a classified memo this spring warning about Jensen Huang's relationship with a suspected spy. Numerous members of Congress have said they will investigate Lutnick's actions and called for him to testify on Capitol Hill. Richard Neal, both Democrats, wrote Lutnick a letter demanding that he preserve all records related to decisions about Nvidia chip exports, pending an investigation. Trump's approval of advanced Nvidia chip exports to China “raises critical questions about whether and to what extent political considerations are improperly influencing policy decisions made by the Administration,” Wyden and Neal wrote. John Kennedy of Louisiana, a member of the Senate Banking Committee, said he has questions for the commerce secretary and urged him to hold a press conference to explain what he knew. “The Commerce Department greenlit $4 billion of sales of advanced chips to the company of the spy that Mr. Huang was having an affair with and I want to know why," Kennedy said. "I want to know why the Commerce Department did it in light of the export controls, and everything I read indicates that this was a decision by the secretary himself." Kennedy added that Lutnick should testify before the Senate and should be subpoenaed if necessary. Huang resigned Thursday after news that he had an affair with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who U.S. intelligence suspects to be a Chinese spy, according to The Times. Last year, Megaspeed was accused of illicitly shipping advanced Nvidia computer chips into China, but in December said there was “no evidence” of such exports. On Thursday, Megaspeed maintained it takes its obligation to comply with American export control laws “extremely seriously” — and that it was committed to working “constructively and transparently” with the U.S. government.

passages: Kennedy is pressing for a Senate committee to question Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent under oath about alleged Chinese access to restricted Nvidia chips, but he announced no hearing or enforcement action.

The dispute centers on Megaspeed International, which the Guardian says facilitated about $12 billion in chip sales that violated U.S. export controls, and allegations that Commerce delayed action despite warnings.
Separately, Bessent says officials are asking Nvidia who was responsible for compliance, putting both federal enforcement decisions and corporate controls under scrutiny.
Kennedy said he was less interested in former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang ’s reported personal conduct than in how U.S. restrictions were apparently bypassed.
He said the administration had contacted the company’s temporary management, lead directors and lawyers as it tried to identify who held that responsibility.
Other administration officials, including Bessent, wanted Megaspeed placed on a trade blacklist, but the Commerce Department stalled enforcement.
That dispute places the department’s decisions—not only Nvidia’s sales practices—under scrutiny.

And if secretary Lutnick is giving our chips away, he needs to stop it, in my opinion.

passages: When it comes to bitcoin, billionaire investor Warren Buffett wants to make one thing clear: Unlike buying stocks, bonds or real estate, buying bitcoin is not an investment.
Don't miss: Here's how much grad school cost when Warren Buffett graduated in 1951, compared to today
"In terms of cryptocurrencies, generally, I can say with almost certainty that they will come to a bad ending ," Buffett told CNBC in January.
"When it happens or how or anything else, I don't know."

For example, "If you buy something [like] a farm, an apartment house or an interest in a business and look to the asset itself to determine whether you've done something — what the farm produces, what the business earns ... it's a perfectly satisfactory investment," Buffett explains to Yahoo Finance .
"[I]f you ban trading in ... bitcoin, which nobody knows exactly what it is, people would say, 'Well why in the world would I buy it?'"
Still, many other investing experts like CNBC's Jim Cramer, Kevin O'Leary and Tony Robbins , also call buying cryptocurrencies a gamble.
They suggest thinking of it like rolling the dice in Las Vegas.

extraction.body: When it comes to bitcoin, billionaire investor Warren Buffett wants to make one thing clear: Unlike buying stocks, bonds or real estate, buying bitcoin is not an investment. That's because it lacks intrinsic value, Buffett says. "If you buy something like bitcoin or some cryptocurrency, you don't have anything that is producing anything," Buffett says in an interview with Yahoo Finance . "You're just hoping the next guy pays more. And you only feel you'll find the next guy to pay more if he thinks he's going to find someone that's going to pay more. "You aren't investing when you do that, you're speculating." Famous for his " buy and hold " investment strategy, the Berkshire Hathaway CEO built his company — and his $82.8 billion net worth — backing companies that have substantive value. "Put together a portfolio of companies whose aggregate earnings march upward over the years, and so also will the portfolio's market value," Buffett wrote in his 1996 letter to shareholders. "If you aren't willing to own a stock for ten years, don't even think about owning it for ten minutes." To be an investment, what you're buying has to be worth something on its own, Buffett says. For example, "If you buy something [like] a farm, an apartment house or an interest in a business and look to the asset itself to determine whether you've done something — what the farm produces, what the business earns ... it's a perfectly satisfactory investment," Buffett explains to Yahoo Finance . "You look at the investment itself to deliver the return to you. "If you ban trading in farms, you could still buy farms, and have a perfectly decent investment," Buffett says. Bitcoin, however, only increases in value by being bought and sold, he argues. Its value comes from what people are willing to pay. "[I]f you ban trading in ... bitcoin, which nobody knows exactly what it is, people would say, 'Well why in the world would I buy it?'" The Oracle of Omaha has held this opinion since at least 2014, when he told CNBC of cryptocurrencies , "It's a mirage basically." "The idea that it has some huge intrinsic value is just a joke in my view," Buffett said. In 2017, bitcoin soared from below $1,000 at the start of the year to over $19,000 in December , catching the attention of everyone from J.P. Morgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon to NFL players. Tuesday, bitcoin traded near $8,900 according to CoinDesk's price index . Buffett sees a bleak future for the digital currency. "In terms of cryptocurrencies, generally, I can say with almost certainty that they will come to a bad ending ," Buffett told CNBC in January. "When it happens or how or anything else, I don't know." Of course, Buffett has been wrong about backing new technologies before. He missed opportunities to invest in Google and Amazon, decisions he now calls mistakes . "I did not think [founder Jeff Bezos] could succeed on the scale he has," Buffett said to shareholders in May 2017. Crypto-enthusiasts argue that Buffet doesn't understand blockchain-based coins, and he has admitted as much. Still, many other investing experts like CNBC's Jim Cramer, Kevin O'Leary and Tony Robbins , also call buying cryptocurrencies a gamble. They suggest thinking of it like rolling the dice in Las Vegas. "As long as you can afford to lose everything you put into it, go with it," O'Leary told CNBC Make It in December, 2017 . "There's nothing wrong with it if you want to gamble [that] somebody else will come along and pay you more money tomorrow," Buffett tells Yahoo Finance. "That's one kind of game. That is not investing." Don't miss: Here's how much grad school cost when Warren Buffett graduated in 1951, compared to today Like this story? Like CNBC Make It on Facebook ! "In terms of cryptocurrencies, generally, I can say with almost certainty that they will come to a bad ending ," Buffett told CNBC in January. "When it happens or how or anything else, I don't know."

Crypto-enthusiasts argue that Buffet doesn't understand blockchain-based coins, and he has admitted as much.

"There's nothing wrong with it if you want to gamble [that] somebody else will come along and pay you more money tomorrow," Buffett tells Yahoo Finance. "That's one kind of game. That is not investing."

For years, Buffett has encouraged everyday investors to consider low-cost funds that track the S&P 500 instead.

On pricing, Buffett’s 2018 remark hasn’t aged well. Since May 7, 2018, the first trading day following his comment, Berkshire’s Class B shares have gained 189.3%. That’s a solid return, but it lags far behind Bitcoin’s 522.4% increase, from $9,769 to $60,801.

Buffett made another significant comment at Berkshire’s annual meeting on April 30, 2022. He stated that he wouldn’t pay $25 for all the Bitcoin in the world, emphasizing that it produces nothing. On that day, Bitcoin closed at $37,821.

Since then, Bitcoin has risen 60.8% from that closing price. However, Berkshire’s Class B shares have outperformed Bitcoin, gaining 79.1% since May 2, 2022. This means that an investor who shared Buffett’s view and chose Berkshire over Bitcoin has seen better returns.

Berkshire, now headed by CEO Greg Abel with Buffett as chairman, has never directly invested in Bitcoin. Its only crypto-related holding was a stake in a Brazilian fintech firm. Berkshire trades at roughly 12 times its earnings, while Bitcoin has no earnings to measure. In the second quarter of 2026, Berkshire also became a net stock buyer for the first time in over three years, investing about $23.5 billion in equities.

Bitcoin, meanwhile, has become accessible to more everyday investors since 2018. Retail investors can buy spot Bitcoin ETFs like the Grayscale Bitcoin Mini Trust ( NYSEARCA: BTC ), which track Bitcoin’s price, using the same apps they use to purchase Berkshire stock.

Buffett has been correct about Bitcoin’s volatility. After his 2018 comment, Bitcoin dropped a staggering 67.1%, falling from $9,769 on May 5, 2018, to $3,216 by December 15, 2018. Although it recovered to $13,034 by June 26, 2019, Bitcoin then fell 51% amid pandemic-driven market turmoil, dropping from $10,318 on February 14, 2020, to $5,054 on March 16, 2020.

Since Buffett’s 2022 comment, Bitcoin reached its all-time high of $126,080, but it trades 51.8% below that peak. The cryptocurrency has repeatedly dropped 50% , highlighting the concerns Buffett has raised. Bitcoin does not pay dividends or generate profits, so its price relies entirely on potential buyers—and those buyers often retreat quickly when panic sets in.
Some market analysts link the November selloff to the debut of a major AI listing, a connection tested in a look at whether the Anthropic IPO is why Bitcoin is crashing .

Buffett was correct about Bitcoin’s price behavior, as shown by its repeated 50% drops, and Berkshire’s 79.1% gain since May 2022 supports his statement. However, when it comes to predicting prices, his 2018 comment—made when Bitcoin was priced at $9,769—missed the mark by a wide margin. Bitcoin’s modest five-year gain of just 4% underscores how much timing affects its returns.

For Bitcoin to catch up to Berkshire’s lead since 2022, it would need to rise to about $67,700, up 11.4% from its current price. If Bitcoin continues to decline and falls below its summer low of $57,700, Buffett’s $25 remark may appear even more accurate over time. Conversely, Standard Chartered expects a much brighter future, projecting Bitcoin could soar to $500,000 by 2030, suggesting significant room for recovery ahead.

passages: For most of the past decade, Wall Street has often treated Warren Buffett's criticism of Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) as the old guard's final word on cryptocurrency.
Whether Buffett was right about Bitcoin largely depends on when the clock starts.
Buffett has been correct about Bitcoin's volatility.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Since Buffett's 2022 comment, Bitcoin reached its all-time high of $126,080, but it trades 51.8% below that peak.
Buffett's 2018 "rat poison squared" jab aged badly on price: Bitcoin has surged 522% since, while Berkshire Class B shares gained 189%.
Berkshire has beaten Bitcoin since Buffett said he wouldn't pay $25 for all the world's Bitcoin, gaining 79% versus 61%.
Despite this growth, Bitcoin's latest decline has strengthened Buffett's supporters.
Berkshire, now headed by CEO Greg Abel with Buffett as chairman, has never directly invested in Bitcoin.
If Bitcoin continues to decline and falls below its summer low of $57,700, Buffett's $25 remark may appear even more accurate over time.
Some market analysts link the November selloff to the debut of a major AI listing, a connection tested in a look at whether the Anthropic IPO is why Bitcoin is crashing.

Despite this growth, Bitcoin's latest decline has strengthened Buffett's supporters. The cryptocurrency slipped below its summer low of about $57,700 during trading on November 21, reaching its lowest point in 16 months. Year to date, Bitcoin is down 31.5% and has declined 26.1% in just the past month. So, how does Buffett's skepticism hold up against Bitcoin's price history since his first remarks? One of Buffett's most famous statements came during Berkshire Hathaway's annual meeting weekend on May 5, 2018, when he told an interviewer that Bitcoin is "probably rat poison squared." On that day, Bitcoin closed at $9,769. His late partner, Charlie Munger, was even more critical at the 2021 meeting, calling cryptocurrency "disgusting and contrary to the interests of civilization." Buffett's main concern centers around cash flow. Unlike a farm or a business, Bitcoin does not generate cash for its owner. Thus, he believes it lacks the productivity of traditional assets. For years, Buffett has encouraged everyday investors to consider low-cost funds that track the S&P 500 instead. On pricing, Buffett's 2018 remark hasn't aged well. Since May 7, 2018, the first trading day following his comment, Berkshire's Class B shares have gained 189.3%. That's a solid return, but it lags far behind Bitcoin's 522.4% increase, from $9,769 to $60,801. Buffett made another significant comment at Berkshire's annual meeting on April 30, 2022. He stated that he wouldn't pay $25 for all the Bitcoin in the world, emphasizing that it produces nothing. On that day, Bitcoin closed at $37,821. Since then, Bitcoin has risen 60.8% from that closing price. However, Berkshire's Class B shares have outperformed Bitcoin, gaining 79.1% since May 2, 2022. This means that an investor who shared Buffett's view and chose Berkshire over Bitcoin has seen better returns. Berkshire, now headed by CEO Greg Abel with Buffett as chairman, has never directly invested in Bitcoin. Its only crypto-related holding was a stake in a Brazilian fintech firm. Berkshire trades at roughly 12 times its earnings, while Bitcoin has no earnings to measure. In the second quarter of 2026, Berkshire also became a net stock buyer for the first time in over three years, investing about $23.5 billion in equities. Bitcoin, meanwhile, has become accessible to more everyday investors since 2018. Retail investors can buy spot Bitcoin ETFs like the Grayscale Bitcoin Mini Trust ( NYSEARCA: BTC ), which track Bitcoin's price, using the same apps they use to purchase Berkshire stock. Buffett has been correct about Bitcoin's volatility. After his 2018 comment, Bitcoin dropped a staggering 67.1%, falling from $9,769 on May 5, 2018, to $3,216 by December 15, 2018. Although it recovered to $13,034 by June 26, 2019, Bitcoin then fell 51% amid pandemic-driven market turmoil, dropping from $10,318 on February 14, 2020, to $5,054 on March 16, 2020. Since Buffett's 2022 comment, Bitcoin reached its all-time high of $126,080, but it trades 51.8% below that peak. The cryptocurrency has repeatedly dropped 50%, highlighting the concerns Buffett has raised. Bitcoin does not pay dividends or generate profits, so its price relies entirely on potential buyers—and those buyers often retreat quickly when panic sets in. Some market analysts link the November selloff to the debut of a major AI listing, a connection tested in a look at whether the Anthropic IPO is why Bitcoin is crashing. Buffett was correct about Bitcoin's price behavior, as shown by its repeated 50% drops, and Berkshire's 79.1% gain since May 2022 supports his statement. Bitcoin's modest five-year gain of just 4% underscores how much timing affects its returns. sources.title: Bessent says Nvidia still owes the administration answers and declines to back a Jensen Huang return - MLQ.ai
passages: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent declined on Sunday, Nov.
22, to endorse a return by Jensen Huang to the top job at Nvidia , saying investigators first need to establish who was responsible for any chip sales that broke US export rules.
"I think we have to see where the buck stops," Bessent said on CBS's "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" when asked whether it would be a good idea for Huang to go back and run the company [1] .
Bessent also said the administration has not received the answers he demanded from Nvidia a week ago.
"We've been in touch with the temporary management, with the lead directors, with their lawyers, and we do need answers" [1] .

On Megaspeed, the Singapore company Alice Huang ran, Bessent said investigators "will see if Megaspeed was indeed a pass-through company, a front company based in Singapore, to get the high-end chips to Chinese entities." He said Nvidia removed Megaspeed from its sales list in August 2025 and that Treasury and other departments have pushed for it to be blacklisted, but called last week's remote-access rule, which stops certain countries and entities from using chips through leased capacity, possibly "more important" [1] .
Huang has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee and will also be interviewed by House panels in early December, CBS News reported [2] .
MLQ.ai has covered his agreement to testify publicly and California's subpoena of Nvidia , which the state attorney general says covers potential criminal violations.

"I think that is kind of a canard," he said, framing the issue as whether Nvidia had a culture of compliance "versus the one person's foibles." Pressed that she was allegedly a Chinese spy, he said: "I assume he didn't know that she was an alleged spy" [1] .

Asked about House Foreign Affairs Committee documents showing Commerce approved sales of more than 800,000 Nvidia and AMD AI chips to China, including to companies linked to the Chinese military, Bessent said the president had drawn a hard line at the H200 and that the buyers were "companies that do business with the Chinese military," not the military itself.
On Friday he told CNBC that no further curbs on older Nvidia chips are needed .
He said he had confidence that Nvidia's board committees "are moving very quickly on this and will come up with some very fulsome and robust answers" [1] .
Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been running the company since Huang resigned, CBS News noted [2] .
He added that the people to examine include whoever ran compliance, "normally, it's the legal department, the general counsel's office" [1] .
Brennan put it to Bessent that President Trump has said Huang should get his job back while Bessent had urged the board to look outside the company for a new chief executive.
Trump said Huang deserved a second chance earlier this week.

On Nvidia's role in AI financing, Bessent called it "one of our great companies" and said that, with the CFO in charge, "I believe that she understands the financing quite well," adding that there is "near unlimited demand for their chips worldwide" [1] .
This article was produced by MLQ.ai's AI newsroom and checked against primary sources such as company filings, official releases and court documents.

extraction.body: Bessent also withheld support for Jensen Huang's return as CEO, saying investigations should conclude before a leader is chosen. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Sunday that Nvidia has yet to explain how its AI chips reached China, and he withheld support for Jensen Huang's return as CEO. The United States is investigating whether Nvidia gave China access to advanced AI chips despite government restrictions, CBS News reported. On Nov. 15, Bessent gave Nvidia 10 days to answer questions about its compliance with export rules in an interview with Fox News. Seven days into that period, Bessent appeared on CBS's "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" and said the administration still lacked the answers it sought. "We don't, Margaret," he said. Officials have contacted Nvidia's interim management, lead directors and lawyers, Bessent said. "It behooves Nvidia to move quickly on this because we want to know what the culture was," he said. "We do need to see who was in charge of compliance there," Bessent said. He also asked, "Was it at the lower levels? Was it at the middle levels? Did it go all the way to the top?". During his Nov. 15 Fox News interview, Bessent raised the possibility of a "culture of noncompliance" at Nvidia and asked whether it was "pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings." He said Sunday that such a culture was only a possibility. "We will see, and that's why I think the board is moving very quickly to establish whether this did or did not exist," he said. Asked about Nvidia's reported "handshake" business approach, Bessent said, "For deals that size, there's no such thing as an untraceable handshake deal." The shipments of chips left financial and documentary trails, he said. "They may not be the 100-page documents, but it will be possible to understand what has gone on here," he said. Bessent said he had confidence that Nvidia's internal committees "will come up with some very fulsome and robust answers." Bessent said the investigations should conclude before Nvidia's next leader is decided. Asked about Huang's return, he said, "I think we have to see where the buck stops," and asked, "Were these malicious actors down at the bottom of the company who were responsible for the noncompliance?". President Donald Trump took a different position at a news conference Friday, saying he wanted Huang to return as chief executive. "I think the company, if they were smart, they'd take that brilliant man, accept an apology and let him go back to work," Trump said earlier. Huang resigned following reports of extramarital affairs, one involving Alice Huang, an alleged spy according to CBS News. The New York Times reported that Huang stepped down after acknowledging an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence had identified as a Chinese asset. Bessent called the affair "kind of a canard" and said company culture mattered more than one person's foibles. "I assume that he didn't know that she was an alleged spy," he said. The Justice and Commerce Departments said last week that they were pursuing a criminal investigation into Megaspeed, a Singapore company Alice Huang once led. Officials are examining whether Megaspeed smuggled Nvidia chips into China, while the Securities and Exchange Commission, or SEC, is investigating Nvidia's accounting practices, according to the Times. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has led Nvidia since Huang's departure. Bessent said last week that he thought Nvidia's leadership needed a major shake-up. He has urged the company to appoint an outsider to run it. It was not immediately known whether Nvidia will deliver the answers before Bessent's 10-day window closes. Huang is scheduled to testify at a private House hearing on Dec. 1; he is also expected to appear before the Senate Banking Committee.

But only older,” he said. Trump also said the US was working on “a very comprehensive deal with China” but gave no details or timeline. He argued that banning all chip sales would push China to make its own chips. His plan would keep China buying older US chips while keeping the most advanced ones in America. These chips are usually seen as AI chips and need US approval before they can be sold to other countries. The new rule, however, removes this option for chip designers in China and other restricted countries. The changes have quickly affected chip companies. According to Reuters , Taiwan’s TSMC stopped taking orders for 16 nanometer and newer chips from some Chinese companies. This left them using older 28 and 40 nanometer technology. Samsung also stopped some chip shipments to China while waiting for US approval. The US has allowed Nvidia to sell its weaker H200 chips to China, but not its more powerful Blackwell chips. “In two years, Blackwell will be obsolete,” Trump stated. For comparison, 16 nanometer chips were among the most advanced in 2015 and were used in Apple’s iPhone 6s. Markets were already falling sharply when Trump made the statement. extraction.body: NEW YORK, Nov 22 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump has made hundreds of millions from his $TRUMP meme coin, but at a Sunday dinner for the token's biggest holders, he said his motive for supporting the cryptocurrency was to boost the economic competitiveness of the ‌United States. "I'm doing it for the United States ... If we don't do it, China's going to do it," Trump told attendees at his ‌golf club outside Washington. It was the third time Trump had held a gala for the top owners of his meme coin, which once soared as high as $75 but has fallen to a record ​low of under $1. The private dinner this year was more low-key than the initial event last year, attendees said, with a smaller crowd and far less money at stake this time. Attendees qualified for the dinner based on their time-weighted holdings of the $TRUMP coin from September 30 to November 16. Organizers indicated that 185 crypto wallets met the criteria for Sunday's dinner, although the leaderboard on the $TRUMP coin club website listed just 130 wallets when the contest concluded on November 16. Together, those listed wallets only held $8.6 million – a ‌shadow of the $148 million listed for the dinner in ⁠May 2025, which was attended by 220 wealthy crypto investors. Sunday's participants stood in the rain as they waited to enter the Trump National club in Sterling, Virginia. Attendees described the scene inside as subdued. It was a far different atmosphere from the first ⁠gala, when tuxedo-clad contest winners pulled up to the club in luxury sports cars, and protesters chanted and stomped outside the club as the presidential Marine One helicopter descended. The May 2025 event's biggest $TRUMP holder was China-born crypto billionaire Justin Sun, who had $18.5 million of the token. This time, there was no Sun at the event signing autographs. Attendees were able to ​dine ​on grilled filet mignon and pan-seared halibut while hearing speeches from the likes of Kevin O'Leary ​of the "Shark Tank" television show and NBA veteran Tristan Thompson. According to the ‌contest's website, the top 29 winners would join a VIP reception with the president and receive a gift bag with Trump swag. The top four also would get an 18-karat gold Trump-branded watch. Morten Christensen, founder of cryptocurrency platform Airdrop Alert, said he qualified for the top 29 with $41,000 of time-weighted $TRUMP holdings by using a hedging strategy – buying and selling the token using perpetual futures – that ensured he did not lose any money. But he was denied a VIP band at the event, Christensen said. "I asked like five people from the staff" and was told to email customer support, he said on Sunday night. "Obviously, no one is going to reply right ‌now," said Christensen, who added that he was kicked out of the event around 7 p.m. ​for "sharing with the press." He waited outside in the rain for his sister, who was still inside. The ​Trump Meme Coin project and the White House did not respond to ​requests for comment. More than half of the digital wallets publicly listed on the contest leaderboard for Sunday's dinner are tied ‌directly to crypto exchanges that bar US-based users, indicating they are linked ​to foreign nationals, according to an analysis ​of blockchain data prepared for Reuters by the nonpartisan, nonprofit consumer advocacy group Public Citizen. The Trump family's other crypto-connected equities and ventures have also fallen in value to record lows. Together, outside investors in their five main crypto and crypto-linked projects have lost more than $5 billion, according to a Reuters analysis. But ​the $TRUMP token has earned the Trump family itself at least $635 ‌million, according to the president's June financial disclosure statement. In total, the Trumps had earned at least $2.3 billion through April from their four main ​crypto ventures, including the meme coin. The president's stake in a fifth crypto-linked venture, Trump Media & Technology Group, is worth about $430 million. (Reporting by Michelle ​Conlin in New York; Editing by Sergio Non, Edmund Klamann and Stephen Coates)

[NEW YORK] US President Donald Trump will headline his third meme coin gala on Sunday night at his country club outside Washington, DC, for top holders of the tokens, which were once worth about US$75 each but are now valued at less than US$1.

Less than 20 months after the first $TRUMP token gala set off a frenzy among 220 wealthy crypto holders vying for spots at the dinner with the president, interest has waned for the latest affair at the Trump National club in Sterling, Virginia.
Organizers indicated that 185 crypto wallets qualified for the dinner, although the leaderboard on the $TRUMP coin club website listed just 130 wallets when the contest concluded on Nov 16.
Together, those listed wallets only held US$8.6 million — a shadow of the US$148 million listed for the first dinner in May 2025, when a time-weighted holding of US$18.5 million grabbed the top seat.

According to the contest’s website, the top 29 winners — which had the highest time-weighted holdings during the contest scoring period from Sep 30 to Nov 16 — will join a VIP reception with the president and receive a gift bag with Trump swag. The top four also get an 18-karat gold Trump-branded watch.
Trump and his family have monetised his brand through an array of equities and crypto ventures during his foray into politics.
Sustainability has reached APAC boardrooms but are board members sufficiently equipped? Find out more in our report.

More than half of the digital wallets publicly listed on the contest leaderboard for Sunday’s dinner are tied directly to crypto exchanges that bar US-based users, indicating they are linked to foreign nationals, according to an analysis of blockchain data prepared for Reuters by the nonpartisan, nonprofit consumer advocacy group Public Citizen.

Democratic leaders in the House and the Senate, where the party won a resounding victory in the midterm elections , have vowed to investigate what they say are unprecedented conflicts of interest posed by the Trump family’s business dealings during Trump’s presidency. They also say they plan to push for legislation that would ban such activities.
The Trump Meme Coin project and the White House did not respond to requests for comment, although the Trump administration has long said the president’s business interests are clean.

“Neither the President nor his family has ever engaged — or will ever engage — in conflicts of interest,” White House spokesperson Anna Kelly told Reuters earlier this year. “President Trump proudly made the United States the crypto capital of the world through executive actions.”

The Trump family’s other crypto-connected equities and ventures have also fallen in value to record lows. Together, outside investors in their five main crypto and crypto-linked projects have lost more than US$5 billion, according to a Reuters analysis.

The Trump meme coin has earned the Trump family at least US$635 million, according to the president’s June financial disclosure statement. In total, the Trumps had earned at least US$2.3 billion through April from their four main crypto ventures, including the meme coin.
The president’s stake in a fifth crypto-linked venture, Trump Media & Technology Group, is worth about US$430 million. REUTERS

extraction.body: NEW YORK, Nov 22 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump has made hundreds of millions from his $TRUMP meme coin, but at a Sunday dinner for the token's biggest holders, he said his motive for supporting the cryptocurrency was to boost the economic competitiveness of the ‌United States. "I'm doing it for the United States ... If we don't do it, China's going to do it," Trump told attendees at his ‌golf club outside Washington. It was the third time Trump had held a gala for the top owners of his meme coin, which once soared as high as $75 but has fallen to a record ​low of under $1. The private dinner this year was more low-key than the initial event last year, attendees said, with a smaller crowd and far less money at stake this time. Attendees qualified for the dinner based on their time-weighted holdings of the $TRUMP coin from September 30 to November 16. Organizers indicated that 185 crypto wallets met the criteria for Sunday's dinner, although the leaderboard on the $TRUMP coin club website listed just 130 wallets when the contest concluded on November 16. Together, those listed wallets only held $8.6 million – a ‌shadow of the $148 million listed for the dinner in ⁠May 2025, which was attended by 220 wealthy crypto investors. Sunday's participants stood in the rain as they waited to enter the Trump National club in Sterling, Virginia. Attendees described the scene inside as subdued. It was a far different atmosphere from the first ⁠gala, when tuxedo-clad contest winners pulled up to the club in luxury sports cars, and protesters chanted and stomped outside the club as the presidential Marine One helicopter descended. The May 2025 event's biggest $TRUMP holder was China-born crypto billionaire Justin Sun, who had $18.5 million of the token. This time, there was no Sun at the event signing autographs. Attendees were able to ​dine ​on grilled filet mignon and pan-seared halibut while hearing speeches from the likes of Kevin O'Leary ​of the "Shark Tank" television show and NBA veteran Tristan Thompson. According to the ‌contest's website, the top 29 winners would join a VIP reception with the president and receive a gift bag with Trump swag. The top four also would get an 18-karat gold Trump-branded watch. Morten Christensen, founder of cryptocurrency platform Airdrop Alert, said he qualified for the top 29 with $41,000 of time-weighted $TRUMP holdings by using a hedging strategy – buying and selling the token using perpetual futures – that ensured he did not lose any money. But he was denied a VIP band at the event, Christensen said. "I asked like five people from the staff" and was told to email customer support, he said on Sunday night. "Obviously, no one is going to reply right ‌now," said Christensen, who added that he was kicked out of the event around 7 p.m. ​for "sharing with the press." He waited outside in the rain for his sister, who was still inside. The ​Trump Meme Coin project and the White House did not respond to ​requests for comment. More than half of the digital wallets publicly listed on the contest leaderboard for Sunday's dinner are tied ‌directly to crypto exchanges that bar US-based users, indicating they are linked ​to foreign nationals, according to an analysis ​of blockchain data prepared for Reuters by the nonpartisan, nonprofit consumer advocacy group Public Citizen. The Trump family's other crypto-connected equities and ventures have also fallen in value to record lows. Together, outside investors in their five main crypto and crypto-linked projects have lost more than $5 billion, according to a Reuters analysis. But ​the $TRUMP token has earned the Trump family itself at least $635 ‌million, according to the president's June financial disclosure statement. In total, the Trumps had earned at least $2.3 billion through April from their four main ​crypto ventures, including the meme coin. The president's stake in a fifth crypto-linked venture, Trump Media & Technology Group, is worth about $430 million. (Reporting by Michelle ​Conlin in New York; Editing by Sergio Non, Edmund Klamann and Stephen Coates)
