extraction.body: When Notable Capital poured roughly 10% of the U.S. portion of its $1 billion-plus fund into Anthropic’s Series E, many limited partners were perplexed by the massive bet. Claude’s maker was still trailing its biggest rival, OpenAI, and DeepSeek had released its R1 model just weeks earlier, threatening to overtake closed-source competitors. Moreover, at $61.5 billion, Anthropic’s valuation was by far the highest that the predominantly early-stage venture firm had invested at in its 25-year history. But investors at Notable, formerly known as GGV Capital before its 2024 split from its China operations, were confident in Anthropic’s future. A team that included managing partners Hans Tung and Glenn Solomon and principal Dan Cahana crunched the numbers and found that developers were increasingly favoring Claude over ChatGPT, using Claude 70% of the time, a reversal from the previous year. “We just knew that for AI, the developer is at the center because they’re the early adopters,” Tung, a co-founder of the firm, told TechCrunch. Having navigated the complexities of U.S.-China relations firsthand, Notable was also convinced that “mission-critical” work would always require U.S.-based, closed-source models, Tung said. Less than two years later, Notable’s LPs are no longer questioning the outsized investment. On Wednesday, Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in the largest IPO in history, reaching a fully diluted valuation of about $1.5 trillion before its shares began trading the next day, a paper return of roughly 15 times. Notable is, of course, not the only firm sitting on a massive paper windfall from Anthropic. Even traditional late-stage investors, who rarely see venture-scale multiples, are set for a big win. Singaporean sovereign wealth fund GIC had been researching Anthropic throughout 2024, but it didn’t make its first investment until after Chris Emanuel, head of the fund’s tech investments, met with Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao at Che Fico, an Italian restaurant in San Francisco, in early 2025. Rao helped pique Emanuel’s interest in the company by showing that model improvements were driving rising enterprise adoption. GIC then made its first investment in Anthropic’s Series F, a round announced in September 2025 at a $183 billion valuation. “Claude Code was just released then,” Emanuel told TechCrunch. “It was very early, but even then, we could see signs that it was really popular with developers.” GIC’s conviction in the AI lab was so high that the fund later led Anthropic’s Series G alongside Coatue at a $380 billion valuation, and returned as one of the co-leads for the pre-IPO round at $965 billion. Across the three rounds, GIC invested more than $4.5 billion in Anthropic, amassing a stake equal to about 1% of the company after its IPO, according to a person familiar with GIC’s financials. Lilian Li, who leads U.S. growth investments at Baillie Gifford, began studying Anthropic and speaking with its team nearly two years before first investing in the company’s Series F. Baillie Gifford invested in the Claude maker once it became clear that the company was “executing consistently” on its vision while generating strong revenue and “compelling gross margins,” Li told TechCrunch. After Baillie Gifford’s initial investment, Anthropic continued to deliver on its promises, expanding into industries such as legal services and life sciences, as well as broader applications like Cowork and cybersecurity, Li said. “It’s actually quite incredible how consistent they have been with how quickly everything’s been changing,” she added. Baillie Gifford went on to invest a total of $1.5 billion across three funding rounds, a bet that has generated substantial paper gains for the investment manager, as well as for dozens of other backers who invested at what once seemed like astronomical valuations. extraction.body: When Notable Capital poured roughly 10% of the U.S. portion of its $1 billion-plus fund into Anthropic’s Series E, many limited partners were perplexed by the massive bet. Claude’s maker was still trailing its biggest rival, OpenAI, and DeepSeek had released its R1 model just weeks earlier, threatening to overtake closed-source competitors. Moreover, at $61.5 billion, Anthropic’s valuation was by far the highest that the predominantly early-stage venture firm had invested at in its 25-year history. But investors at Notable, formerly known as GGV Capital before its 2024 split from its China operations, were confident in Anthropic’s future. A team that included managing partners Hans Tung and Glenn Solomon and principal Dan Cahana crunched the numbers and found that developers were increasingly favoring Claude over ChatGPT, using Claude 70% of the time, a reversal from the previous year. “We just knew that for AI, the developer is at the center because they’re the early adopters,” Tung, a co-founder of the firm, told TechCrunch. Having navigated the complexities of U.S.-China relations firsthand, Notable was also convinced that “mission-critical” work would always require U.S.-based, closed-source models, Tung said. Less than two years later, Notable’s LPs are no longer questioning the outsized investment. On Wednesday, Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in the largest IPO in history, reaching a fully diluted valuation of about $1.5 trillion before its shares began trading the next day, a paper return of roughly 15 times. Notable is, of course, not the only firm sitting on a massive paper windfall from Anthropic. Even traditional late-stage investors, who rarely see venture-scale multiples, are set for a big win. Singaporean sovereign wealth fund GIC had been researching Anthropic throughout 2024, but it didn’t make its first investment until after Chris Emanuel, head of the fund’s tech investments, met with Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao at Che Fico, an Italian restaurant in San Francisco, in early 2025. Rao helped pique Emanuel’s interest in the company by showing that model improvements were driving rising enterprise adoption. GIC then made its first investment in Anthropic’s Series F, a round announced in September 2025 at a $183 billion valuation. “Claude Code was just released then,” Emanuel told TechCrunch. “It was very early, but even then, we could see signs that it was really popular with developers.” GIC’s conviction in the AI lab was so high that the fund later led Anthropic’s Series G alongside Coatue at a $380 billion valuation, and returned as one of the co-leads for the pre-IPO round at $965 billion. Across the three rounds, GIC invested more than $4.5 billion in Anthropic, amassing a stake equal to about 1% of the company after its IPO, according to a person familiar with GIC’s financials. Lilian Li, who leads U.S. growth investments at Baillie Gifford, began studying Anthropic and speaking with its team nearly two years before first investing in the company’s Series F. Baillie Gifford invested in the Claude maker once it became clear that the company was “executing consistently” on its vision while generating strong revenue and “compelling gross margins,” Li told TechCrunch. After Baillie Gifford’s initial investment, Anthropic continued to deliver on its promises, expanding into industries such as legal services and life sciences, as well as broader applications like Cowork and cybersecurity, Li said. “It’s actually quite incredible how consistent they have been with how quickly everything’s been changing,” she added. Baillie Gifford went on to invest a total of $1.5 billion across three funding rounds, a bet that has generated substantial paper gains for the investment manager, as well as for dozens of other backers who invested at what once seemed like astronomical valuations. extraction.body: Some of these apps will be familiar, while others you may not have heard of. Android Auto users typically utilize just a few basic apps like Google Maps for directions and Spotify for music. They don't dive into the developer menu ; they don't make any serious changes to the way Android Auto works; and they don't know they could be spending all those minutes waiting for someone in a parking lot playing games directly on the car's infotainment display . But the platform's compatible app library runs much deeper, well beyond navigation and streaming. Android Auto actually supports a surprising range of communication and meeting tools, like WhatsApp and Google Meet, and even a bunch of other apps to help you navigate more efficiently. Each one adds layer after layer of functionality that most users never think to explore. Discovering new apps can genuinely change how you commute while also making it possible to enjoy your drive just a tiny bit more. Android Auto comes with some extra functionality for those in the corporate world, as several popular apps come with Android Auto support for meetings and calls, with Google Meet leading the way. Because Meet is Google's own app, it fits naturally into the Android Auto experience. You can see your upcoming meetings on the car display and join a call with a single tap, all in audio-only mode so your eyes stay on the road. Whether it's a short check-in with your manager or a longer team call, Meet makes it easy to keep up with your schedule even if you have to drive around. Google's app isn't the only option, though. Zoom, Webex by Cisco and Microsoft Teams all work on Android Auto, offering users the opportunity to join video conferences with audio only. Some apps take integration a step further. Microsoft Teams, for instance, lets users check their calendar and place calls directly from the car display. Google Meet also displays upcoming meetings on your schedule. These features are particularly useful if you're often traveling from location to location but still have to participate in meetings along the way. They also help if you have to leave early to pick up the kids from school while a meeting is still on your calendar. One thing to mention about these apps is that, depending on your employer, restrictions may apply. Certain companies require corporate apps like Google Meet and Microsoft Teams to run inside an isolated Android Work Profile. In such situations, Android Auto may block calendar sync or prevent the app from appearing on the screen. There's a Work Mode in the works on Android Auto , though, so it may soon be easier to reach all those apps that are locked out by your employer. With gas prices being what they are these days, it's more important than ever to know where to fuel up. Apps like Fuelio can help with that when you're looking for a place to put gas in your car without breaking the bank. Fuelio tracks fill-ups, odometer readings and fuel prices, then calculates your average fuel economy and cost per mile over time. You can even use various filters to display gas stations that were updated within the past day, or those that are most appreciated by users. Google Maps and other similar tools can surface the nearest gas stations and even tell you the latest prices, but Fuelio gives more in-depth information regarding fuel type, distance and more. Plus, when you throw in all the other features, it's a much better fit if you want to know exactly how much your car is costing you. While Fuelio is free to use with Android Auto, there is a premium version available that costs money. If you're driving an EV, then the app you absolutely must use through Android Auto is PlugShare . This free tool (the paid version removes ads) gives you access to a crowd-sourced map that lets you see the nearest charging stations along your route. Its real strength is the community behind it, because drivers leave real-time feedback, uploading photos of the charger layout, reporting broken plugs and checking in after charging. That gives you a clear picture of what to expect before you pull in, so a station that looks fine on paper but has been out of service for days won't catch you off guard. There are loads of filters you can play with, letting you choose the exact plug type, charging speed and network. You can also check which amenities are nearby, such as restrooms or a place to grab coffee while you wait. It's also a great tool for long-distance drives, as it automatically recommends charging stops along the way based on your specific EV model's range. That goes a long way toward easing the range anxiety that comes with getting an electric car. The one downside is that the data is only as good as its contributors, so stations in less-traveled areas may have fewer recent reports. Data can be expensive, especially if you use your phone a ton. When you're traveling abroad, costs go up by quite a bit, so you should make the most of your home Wi-Fi. Apps like HERE WeGo through Android Auto offer offline navigation, so your data plan isn't ever a concern. HERE WeGo lets you download maps for entire countries so you always know where you're going. For some countries, you can download maps for certain areas, such as for Germany where you can grab a map for Berlin and another for Hamburg. In the United States, you can grab maps for entire states, but not separate cities. There are plenty of features to fiddle with to make this app yours, like choosing which fuel type your car uses, having the metric vs. imperial system displayed the way you prefer and so on. The app will flag parking spots and rest areas along the route, and you can even tell it what types of things to avoid. For instance, Waze lets you avoid ferries and highways, but HERE WeGo can have you avoid tunnels and U-turns too. The app can take things one step further and even use visual references on route, which means it will tell you to make a right at the traffic light or when you reach a certain landmark. But the platform's compatible app library runs much deeper, well beyond navigation and streaming.

Android Auto actually supports a surprising range of communication and meeting tools, like WhatsApp and Google Meet, and even a bunch of other apps to help you navigate more efficiently. Each one adds layer after layer of functionality that most users never think to explore. You can see your upcoming meetings on the car display and join a call with a single tap, all in audio-only mode so your eyes stay on the road. sources.title: Interest in Trump’s meme coin dinner fades as $TRUMP sinks to record lows - Yahoo Finance
passages: Today, interest in the third meme coin dinner ​contest has collapsed.
It invited 185 holders of the token, known as $TRUMP, to register and see who held the largest amounts during the contest scoring period from September 30 to November 16.
The leaderboard at closing showed only 130 crypto wallets — holding a combined $8.6 million — a 94% drop from the first dinner.
The contest's muted results come at a time when the Trump family's other crypto-connected equities and ventures have also deflated to record lows.
Together, outside investors in ​the ​five main crypto and crypto-linked projects have lost more than $5 billion, according to Reuters estimates.

NEW YORK, Nov 16 (Reuters) - As winners were being determined on Monday for President Donald Trump's third crypto gala dinner, scheduled for November 22 at his golf club outside Washington, the president's meme coin was trading near 92 cents, a bruising tumble from its high ‌in 2025 of more than $74.
In total, a Reuters analysis found that the Trumps have earned at least $2.3 billion through ​April from their four main crypto ventures, including the meme coin.

Wealthy ‌crypto investors collectively wagered $148 million on what the president promoted as the "most EXCLUSIVE INVITATION in the world." The holdings needed to win a seat at the dinner ranged from $59,000 to $18.5 million.
The Trump meme coin project and the Trump Organization did not respond to a request for comment.
He ⁠came in at 26th on the leaderboard with about $41,000 in time-weighted Trump token holdings.
His 23-year-old sister, Gabrielle Felen, is also coming along.
She was disappointed she did not make the top 120 — now, she will not get the gift bag.
Most of those losses ​came before the midterm elections in which the Democrats dealt a heavy ‌defeat to Trump's Republican Party, a result that sent prices even lower.

extraction.body: NEW YORK, Nov 16 (Reuters) - As winners were being determined on Monday for President Donald Trump's third crypto gala dinner, scheduled for November 22 at his golf club outside Washington, the president's meme coin was trading near 92 cents, a bruising tumble from its high ‌in 2025 of more than $74. At the peak of Trump's popularity, the token's price surged more than 60% when the first contest was announced in April 2025. Wealthy ‌crypto investors collectively wagered $148 million on what the president promoted as the "most EXCLUSIVE INVITATION in the world." The holdings needed to win a seat at the dinner ranged from $59,000 to $18.5 million. Today, interest in the third meme coin dinner ​contest has collapsed. It invited 185 holders of the token, known as $TRUMP, to register and see who held the largest amounts during the contest scoring period from September 30 to November 16. The leaderboard at closing showed only 130 crypto wallets — holding a combined $8.6 million — a 94% drop from the first dinner. The top 29 wallets will be awarded a "Special VIP Reception" with "YOUR FAVORITE PRESIDENT," according to the contest's website, along with VIP seating at the dinner. This will be the third time Morten Christensen, a crypto entrepreneur from the Netherlands, has qualified for the dinner, but the first where ‌he will be at the VIP reception with the president. He ⁠came in at 26th on the leaderboard with about $41,000 in time-weighted Trump token holdings. "You can be in a room with the president of the United States, arguably one of the most powerful people in the world," said Christensen. "So why would I not go if it cost me ⁠almost nothing to go?" His 23-year-old sister, Gabrielle Felen, is also coming along. She bought about 2,000 Trump tokens. She was disappointed she did not make the top 120 — now, she will not get the gift bag. The contest's muted results come at a time when the Trump family's other crypto-connected equities and ventures have also deflated to record lows. Together, outside investors in ​the ​five main crypto and crypto-linked projects have lost more than $5 billion, according to Reuters estimates. Most of those losses ​came before the midterm elections in which the Democrats dealt a heavy ‌defeat to Trump's Republican Party, a result that sent prices even lower. Because the price of the Trump token has continued to fall sharply during the holding period in the run-up to the dinner, the winners have lost millions of dollars in recent weeks. The Trump meme coin project and the Trump Organization did not respond to a request for comment. The White House also did not respond to a request for comment but has repeatedly said there is no conflict of interest because the president's assets are in a trust run by his children. While most buyers have been left with losses, the Trump meme coin has so far earned the Trump family at least $635 million, according to the president's June ‌financial disclosure statement. In total, a Reuters analysis found that the Trumps have earned at least $2.3 billion through ​April from their four main crypto ventures, including the meme coin. The president's stake in the fifth crypto-linked ​venture, Trump Media & Technology Group, is worth about $500 million. The billions the Trump family ​has earned while in office have drawn opposition from congressional Democrats, who retook control of both the US Senate and US House of Representatives in the midterm ‌elections. They will now have subpoena power and the ability to ​launch investigations and conduct hearings about what US ​Senator Elizabeth Warren, a Massachusetts Democrat who will lead oversight on the Senate Banking Committee, has characterized as "an orgy of corruption." Warren said last Monday that the Trump family crypto businesses will be a focus of her accountability investigations. Crypto wallets are anonymous and known only by strings of letters and numbers. The anonymity is what ​prompted government ethics officials to raise concern about the first two ‌dinners because they said the meme coin could be a conduit for anonymous foreign individuals looking to purchase access to the president. Blockchain analysis showed that ​of the 220 wallets that competed in the first contest, more than half were likely based outside the United States. (Reporting by Michelle Conlin in New ​York and Tom Bergin in London; Editing by Tom Lasseter, Matthew Lewis and Nick Zieminski)

passages: CryptoPotato reported that Trump’s first dinner in May 2025 was limited to the top 220 holders, with the leading 25 receiving an additional reception and VIP experiences.
The announcement initially sent the token flying, even after it had crumbled at the time.
Reports and Wu Blockchain noted that the POTUS will host the dinner for top TRUMP holders even as the number of participants has declined sharply.

Crypto Trader Morten Christensen told Bloomberg that hedging his holdings reduced his effective cost of qualifying from roughly $1,200 for the first dinner and $500 for the second to an approximately $6 profit this time.
Coin Bureau highlighted an even more striking comparison, with one participant reportedly securing a place after buying only $518 worth of the meme coin.
Reuters reported that only 130 wallets made the final leaderboard this time, collectively holding $8.6 million worth of TRUMP.
The newest event has at least 5,000 wallets eligible to participate but never registered, even after organizers extended the deadline by four days.
This significant decline in demand has mimicked the underlying asset’s performance to a large extent.
TRUMP currently trades well below $1 after peaking at $74-$75 shortly following its January 2025 launch.
This means that the asset has lost almost 99% of its value in less than two years.
The second gala announced for April 2026 produced a similar immediate reaction.
TRUMP surged more than 50% from its then-ATL after organizers invited the top 297 holders to an event at Mar-a-Lago, with 29 qualifying for a VIP reception.
According to some reports, participants have qualified for just $518 now, while thousands of eligible wallets never even registered, as TRUMP continues to lose value.

coreStoryFacts.text: Today, interest in the third meme coin dinner ​contest has collapsed.
It invited 185 holders of the token, known as $TRUMP, to register and see who held the largest amounts during the contest scoring period from September 30 to November 16.
The leaderboard at closing showed only 130 crypto wallets — holding a combined $8.6 million — a 94% drop from the first dinner.
The contest's muted results come at a time when the Trump family's other crypto-connected equities and ventures have also deflated to record lows.
Together, outside investors in ​the ​five main crypto and crypto-linked projects have lost more than $5 billion, according to Reuters estimates.

NEW YORK, Nov 16 (Reuters) - As winners were being determined on Monday for President Donald Trump's third crypto gala dinner, scheduled for November 22 at his golf club outside Washington, the president's meme coin was trading near 92 cents, a bruising tumble from its high ‌in 2025 of more than $74.
In total, a Reuters analysis found that the Trumps have earned at least $2.3 billion through ​April from their four main crypto ventures, including the meme coin.

Wealthy ‌crypto investors collectively wagered $148 million on what the president promoted as the "most EXCLUSIVE INVITATION in the world." The holdings needed to win a seat at the dinner ranged from $59,000 to $18.5 million.
The Trump meme coin project and the Trump Organization did not respond to a request for comment.
He ⁠came in at 26th on the leaderboard with about $41,000 in time-weighted Trump token holdings.
His 23-year-old sister, Gabrielle Felen, is also coming along.
She was disappointed she did not make the top 120 — now, she will not get the gift bag.
Most of those losses ​came before the midterm elections in which the Democrats dealt a heavy ‌defeat to Trump's Republican Party, a result that sent prices even lower.
The president presided over an upscale dinner for investors in his collapsing meme coin, celebrating the venture even as the price of admission has plummeted.
A pump-up dancer in a Trump mask greeted them.

VIP guests received gold-tone Trump diver watches and Trump-branded “Victory” fragrances at his Northern Virginia golf club, where they rubbed shoulders with retired athletes Floyd Mayweather and Tristan Thompson.
Mentalist Lior Suchard claimed to read their minds.
In a reception room here where chandeliers abounded and women less so, top collectors of President Donald Trump’s novelty crypto token gathered to graze on fall harvest salad and filet mignon.

At the peak of Trump's popularity, the token's price surged more than 60% when the first contest was announced in April 2025. Wealthy ‌crypto investors collectively wagered $148 million on what the president promoted as the "most EXCLUSIVE INVITATION in the world." The holdings needed to win a seat at the dinner ranged from $59,000 to $18.5 million. Today, interest in the third meme coin dinner ​contest has collapsed. It invited 185 holders of the token, known as $TRUMP, to register and see who held the largest amounts during the contest scoring period from September 30 to November 16. The leaderboard at closing showed only 130 crypto wallets — holding a combined $8.6 million — a 94% drop from the first dinner. The top 29 wallets will be awarded a "Special VIP Reception" with "YOUR FAVORITE PRESIDENT," according to the contest's website, along with VIP seating at the dinner. This will be the third time Morten Christensen, a crypto entrepreneur from the Netherlands, has qualified for the dinner, but the first where ‌he will be at the VIP reception with the president. He ⁠came in at 26th on the leaderboard with about $41,000 in time-weighted Trump token holdings. "You can be in a room with the president of the United States, arguably one of the most powerful people in the world," said Christensen. "So why would I not go if it cost me ⁠almost nothing to go?" His 23-year-old sister, Gabrielle Felen, is also coming along. She bought about 2,000 Trump tokens. She was disappointed she did not make the top 120 — now, she will not get the gift bag. The contest's muted results come at a time when the Trump family's other crypto-connected equities and ventures have also deflated to record lows. Together, outside investors in ​the ​five main crypto and crypto-linked projects have lost more than $5 billion, according to Reuters estimates. Most of those losses ​came before the midterm elections in which the Democrats dealt a heavy ‌defeat to Trump's Republican Party, a result that sent prices even lower. Because the price of the Trump token has continued to fall sharply during the holding period in the run-up to the dinner, the winners have lost millions of dollars in recent weeks. The Trump meme coin project and the Trump Organization did not respond to a request for comment. The White House also did not respond to a request for comment but has repeatedly said there is no conflict of interest because the president's assets are in a trust run by his children. While most buyers have been left with losses, the Trump meme coin has so far earned the Trump family at least $635 million, according to the president's June ‌financial disclosure statement. In total, a Reuters analysis found that the Trumps have earned at least $2.3 billion through ​April from their four main crypto ventures, including the meme coin. The president's stake in the fifth crypto-linked ​venture, Trump Media & Technology Group, is worth about $500 million. The billions the Trump family ​has earned while in office have drawn opposition from congressional Democrats, who retook control of both the US Senate and US House of Representatives in the midterm ‌elections. They will now have subpoena power and the ability to ​launch investigations and conduct hearings about what US ​Senator Elizabeth Warren, a Massachusetts Democrat who will lead oversight on the Senate Banking Committee, has characterized as "an orgy of corruption." Warren said last Monday that the Trump family crypto businesses will be a focus of her accountability investigations. Crypto wallets are anonymous and known only by strings of letters and numbers. The anonymity is what ​prompted government ethics officials to raise concern about the first two ‌dinners because they said the meme coin could be a conduit for anonymous foreign individuals looking to purchase access to the president. Blockchain analysis showed that ​of the 220 wallets that competed in the first contest, more than half were likely based outside the United States. sources.title: Berkshire's $358 Billion Portfolio Now Leans on AI: Three Holdings Make Up 41.6% - BigGo Finance
passages: Berkshire Hathaway's equity portfolio has quietly become a wager on artificial intelligence, even though its most famous investor spent decades avoiding the hottest technology trends.

Three of the conglomerate's largest holdings - Apple, Coca-Cola and Alphabet - now account for 41.6% of a stock book valued at roughly $358 billion, and each is using AI to sharpen an established business rather than betting the company on it.
The company's pitch to investors is distribution: with more than 2.5 billion active devices in use worldwide, it can push AI features to consumers at a scale few rivals can match.
Its Apple Intelligence suite includes writing tools that draft and summarize messages, notification sorting and an upgraded Safari browser that can flag changes to web pages a user is tracking.
Berkshire spent about $38 billion building the stake between 2016 and 2023, and it was worth more than $170 billion by early 2024.
Because it had grown to more than half the portfolio, Buffett's team sold 75% of the position by the end of 2025 to bank gains and cut concentration risk.
Berkshire paid about $1.3 billion for 400 million shares between 1988 and 1994 and has never sold one; the stake is worth $39.5 billion and will generate $848 million in dividends this year.

The beverage maker has leaned on technology to manage a portfolio of roughly 200 brands across more than 200 countries, and in 2024 it agreed to spend $1.1 billion over five years on Microsoft's Azure cloud platform, giving it access to tools including the Copilot assistant.
Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode features are generating answers above traditional search results, which the company says is lifting search usage and pushing advertising revenue to records.
Google Cloud, meanwhile, grew revenue 103% in the quarter ended Sept.
30 and carries a $561 billion order backlog from customers waiting for more data-center capacity.
The three positions were assembled under his watch, but it is his successor, Greg Abel, who has been adding to them.
Abel took over as chief executive at the start of the year, and his most aggressive move has been in Alphabet, where Berkshire's stake has grown roughly sixfold.
Abel's buying has been concentrated in that last name.
According to The Motley Fool, he deployed an estimated $28 billion into Alphabet in the first half of 2026, including a $10 billion private placement priced at $355 a share.
He then paused in the third quarter, even as the stock traded around $340 and later fell to about $280 - below what Berkshire had paid.
The shares now change hands at roughly 21 times forward earnings.
Alphabet's weighting, while smaller, has become large enough that adding further may raise the bar for Abel, since each purchase increases portfolio concentration.
The pause last quarter suggests that calculus is already part of his thinking.
For Berkshire shareholders, the practical question is whether these three businesses can keep compounding without the companies having to win the AI race outright.
Whether that approach produces the returns that made Berkshire a $1 trillion company will now be Abel's test to meet.

Three of the conglomerate's largest holdings - Apple, Coca-Cola and Alphabet - now account for 41.6% of a stock book valued at roughly $358 billion, and each is using AI to sharpen an established business rather than betting the company on it. The shift is notable because Warren Buffett, who ran Berkshire from 1965 until stepping down at the end of 2025, built his reputation on steady earnings and predictable management teams. The three positions were assembled under his watch, but it is his successor, Greg Abel, who has been adding to them. Abel took over as chief executive at the start of the year, and his most aggressive move has been in Alphabet, where Berkshire's stake has grown roughly sixfold. Berkshire's largest single position remains Apple, at 22.4% of the portfolio. The company's pitch to investors is distribution: with more than 2.5 billion active devices in use worldwide, it can push AI features to consumers at a scale few rivals can match. Its Apple Intelligence suite includes writing tools that draft and summarize messages, notification sorting and an upgraded Safari browser that can flag changes to web pages a user is tracking. Berkshire spent about $38 billion building the stake between 2016 and 2023, and it was worth more than $170 billion by early 2024. Because it had grown to more than half the portfolio, Buffett's team sold 75% of the position by the end of 2025 to bank gains and cut concentration risk. Coca-Cola, at 11%, is the oldest of the three. Berkshire paid about $1.3 billion for 400 million shares between 1988 and 1994 and has never sold one; the stake is worth $39.5 billion and will generate $848 million in dividends this year. The beverage maker has leaned on technology to manage a portfolio of roughly 200 brands across more than 200 countries, and in 2024 it agreed to spend $1.1 billion over five years on Microsoft's Azure cloud platform, giving it access to tools including the Copilot assistant. The newest and fastest-moving piece is Alphabet, at 8.2% of the portfolio. Berkshire first bought the stock in the third quarter of 2025, and the position now stands at 78.8 million Class A shares and 27.2 million Class C shares worth a combined $29.6 billion. Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode features are generating answers above traditional search results, which the company says is lifting search usage and pushing advertising revenue to records. Google Cloud, meanwhile, grew revenue 103% in the quarter ended Sept. 30 and carries a $561 billion order backlog from customers waiting for more data-center capacity. Abel's buying has been concentrated in that last name. According to The Motley Fool, he deployed an estimated $28 billion into Alphabet in the first half of 2026, including a $10 billion private placement priced at $355 a share. He then paused in the third quarter, even as the stock traded around $340 and later fell to about $280 - below what Berkshire had paid. The shares now change hands at roughly 21 times forward earnings. The rationale Buffett laid out in an interview this summer was return on invested capital: Alphabet can pour enormous sums into AI infrastructure and earn a high return doing so, which should produce exceptional cash flow over time. Google Cloud chief executive Thomas Kurian has said the average server on its platform pays for itself in about two years, while its custom TPU systems do so in half that time. As a larger share of capital spending goes toward revenue-generating servers and toward in-house hardware, the payback math improves. Note: Portfolio weights and values are as of the latest reporting cited; Alphabet's cloud growth refers to the quarter ended Sept. 30. The concentration cuts both ways. Apple alone represents nearly a quarter of the stock book, so a stumble in its consumer AI rollout would leave a visible mark on Berkshire's results. Alphabet's weighting, while smaller, has become large enough that adding further may raise the bar for Abel, since each purchase increases portfolio concentration. The pause last quarter suggests that calculus is already part of his thinking. For Berkshire shareholders, the practical question is whether these three businesses can keep compounding without the companies having to win the AI race outright. Each is using the technology to defend an existing franchise - search advertising, beverages, hardware - rather than to create a new one, which fits the Buffett template of reliable profits and experienced management. Whether that approach produces the returns that made Berkshire a $1 trillion company will now be Abel's test to meet. Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » Warren Buffett's successor has given Berkshire's portfolio a tech focus. Image source: Getty Images. iPhone maker Apple has been Berkshire's No. 1 holding for more than a decade. When Warren Buffett initially began buying shares of Apple in early 2016, he valued the loyalty of its customer base and its exceptional pricing power above all else. Later on, the Oracle of Omaha came to appreciate Apple's market-leading share repurchase program. But Apple is about much more than just selling tech devices. Under now-retired CEO Tim Cook, it became a platforms company that generates steady growth from an assortment of loyalty-enhancing subscription services. Apple Intelligence is another long-term growth driver. The company's generative AI platform, integrated into its new devices, is tasked with being a virtual assistant for users. Apple Intelligence should boost demand for iPhone, Mac, and iPad. Whereas Apple's investments in artificial intelligence are rather tame for a company of its size, Google parent Alphabet is spending a small fortune on the AI data center build-out. It's the company's AI ambitions that have encouraged Berkshire's new boss to pile in since the beginning of the year. Since integrating generative AI and large language model solutions into Google Cloud, the world's No. 3 cloud infrastructure services platform by total spend, sales for this considerably higher-margin segment have gone parabolic. Google Cloud's revenue more than doubled in the third quarter to $30.7 billion. Despite the focus being on AI, Alphabet maintains its virtual monopoly on internet search. As of October 2026, Google accounted for more than 91% of worldwide internet search share, according to GlobalStats, affording Alphabet exceptional ad-pricing power. The third game-changing AI stock, which collectively accounts for 31% of Berkshire Hathaway's invested assets, is the newest addition: Bending Spoons. Bending Spoons is a tech-driven merger-and-acquisition company that uses its proprietary software, AI, and other tools to improve the operating efficiency of the established businesses it acquires. It's made several acquisitions thus far, with AOL and Vimeo the best-known, and often seeks out low-cost, high-margin, subscription-driven businesses. According to Berkshire's latest 13F, Abel oversaw the purchase of nearly 20.7 million shares of Bending Spoons at its July initial public offering, and has since added 10 million more shares from a private placement at $33 per share. passages: Berkshire Hathaway's equity portfolio has quietly become a wager on artificial intelligence, even though its most famous investor spent decades avoiding the hottest technology trends.

Three of the conglomerate's largest holdings - Apple, Coca-Cola and Alphabet - now account for 41.6% of a stock book valued at roughly $358 billion, and each is using AI to sharpen an established business rather than betting the company on it.
The company's pitch to investors is distribution: with more than 2.5 billion active devices in use worldwide, it can push AI features to consumers at a scale few rivals can match.
Its Apple Intelligence suite includes writing tools that draft and summarize messages, notification sorting and an upgraded Safari browser that can flag changes to web pages a user is tracking.
Berkshire spent about $38 billion building the stake between 2016 and 2023, and it was worth more than $170 billion by early 2024.
Because it had grown to more than half the portfolio, Buffett's team sold 75% of the position by the end of 2025 to bank gains and cut concentration risk.
Berkshire paid about $1.3 billion for 400 million shares between 1988 and 1994 and has never sold one; the stake is worth $39.5 billion and will generate $848 million in dividends this year.

The beverage maker has leaned on technology to manage a portfolio of roughly 200 brands across more than 200 countries, and in 2024 it agreed to spend $1.1 billion over five years on Microsoft's Azure cloud platform, giving it access to tools including the Copilot assistant.
Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode features are generating answers above traditional search results, which the company says is lifting search usage and pushing advertising revenue to records.
Google Cloud, meanwhile, grew revenue 103% in the quarter ended Sept.
30 and carries a $561 billion order backlog from customers waiting for more data-center capacity.
The three positions were assembled under his watch, but it is his successor, Greg Abel, who has been adding to them.
Abel took over as chief executive at the start of the year, and his most aggressive move has been in Alphabet, where Berkshire's stake has grown roughly sixfold.
Abel's buying has been concentrated in that last name.
According to The Motley Fool, he deployed an estimated $28 billion into Alphabet in the first half of 2026, including a $10 billion private placement priced at $355 a share.
He then paused in the third quarter, even as the stock traded around $340 and later fell to about $280 - below what Berkshire had paid.
The shares now change hands at roughly 21 times forward earnings.
Alphabet's weighting, while smaller, has become large enough that adding further may raise the bar for Abel, since each purchase increases portfolio concentration.
The pause last quarter suggests that calculus is already part of his thinking.
For Berkshire shareholders, the practical question is whether these three businesses can keep compounding without the companies having to win the AI race outright.
Whether that approach produces the returns that made Berkshire a $1 trillion company will now be Abel's test to meet.

facts.text: This has been a year of immense change for Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE:BRKA)(NYSE:BRKB) and its shareholders.

At the end of 2025, Warren Buffett , the company's longtime leader, retired as CEO, paving the way for his protégé, Greg Abel, to take over Berkshire's day-to-day operations and the oversight of its $363 billion portfolio.
Abel took just a few months to completely reshape this portfolio .
In particular, artificial intelligence (AI) stocks are on the menu in a way that was never seen under the Oracle of Omaha.

Based on Berkshire's newly released Form 13F, three game-changing AI stocks -- Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL), Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL)(NASDAQ:GOOG), and Bending Spoons (NASDAQ:BSP) -- now comprise 31% ($111.7 billion) of invested assets.

3 cloud infrastructure services platform by total spend, sales for this considerably higher-margin segment have gone parabolic.
Google Cloud's revenue more than doubled in the third quarter to $30.7 billion.

Berkshire Hathaway's equity portfolio has quietly become a wager on artificial intelligence, even though its most famous investor spent decades avoiding the hottest technology trends.

Three of the conglomerate's largest holdings - Apple, Coca-Cola and Alphabet - now account for 41.6% of a stock book valued at roughly $358 billion, and each is using AI to sharpen an established business rather than betting the company on it.
The company's pitch to investors is distribution: with more than 2.5 billion active devices in use worldwide, it can push AI features to consumers at a scale few rivals can match.
Its Apple Intelligence suite includes writing tools that draft and summarize messages, notification sorting and an upgraded Safari browser that can flag changes to web pages a user is tracking.
Berkshire spent about $38 billion building the stake between 2016 and 2023, and it was worth more than $170 billion by early 2024.
Because it had grown to more than half the portfolio, Buffett's team sold 75% of the position by the end of 2025 to bank gains and cut concentration risk.
Berkshire paid about $1.3 billion for 400 million shares between 1988 and 1994 and has never sold one; the stake is worth $39.5 billion and will generate $848 million in dividends this year.

The beverage maker has leaned on technology to manage a portfolio of roughly 200 brands across more than 200 countries, and in 2024 it agreed to spend $1.1 billion over five years on Microsoft's Azure cloud platform, giving it access to tools including the Copilot assistant.
Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode features are generating answers above traditional search results, which the company says is lifting search usage and pushing advertising revenue to records.
Google Cloud, meanwhile, grew revenue 103% in the quarter ended Sept.
30 and carries a $561 billion order backlog from customers waiting for more data-center capacity.
The three positions were assembled under his watch, but it is his successor, Greg Abel, who has been adding to them.
Abel took over as chief executive at the start of the year, and his most aggressive move has been in Alphabet, where Berkshire's stake has grown roughly sixfold.
Abel's buying has been concentrated in that last name.
According to The Motley Fool, he deployed an estimated $28 billion into Alphabet in the first half of 2026, including a $10 billion private placement priced at $355 a share.
He then paused in the third quarter, even as the stock traded around $340 and later fell to about $280 - below what Berkshire had paid.
The shares now change hands at roughly 21 times forward earnings.
Alphabet's weighting, while smaller, has become large enough that adding further may raise the bar for Abel, since each purchase increases portfolio concentration.
The pause last quarter suggests that calculus is already part of his thinking.
For Berkshire shareholders, the practical question is whether these three businesses can keep compounding without the companies having to win the AI race outright.
Whether that approach produces the returns that made Berkshire a $1 trillion company will now be Abel's test to meet.

The settings for a laptop’s touchpad can be a touchy issue: Not everyone right-clicks as often, taps the touchpad with the same degree of force or scrolls as swiftly. Windows 11 offers a remarkable degree of control over how a touchpad will work, and these controls actually work the same across laptops from different manufacturers.

AP-Yonhap WASHINGTON — Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Friday he was frustrated with the Commerce Department’s delay in implementing restrictions over the export of certain Nvidia chips to China. Bessent said on CNBC that his department, along with the departments of State and Defense and the U.S. Trade Representative, were in favor of adding Megaspeed to an export control list for months but that the Commerce Department was in charge of the matter. “I am frustrated when President Trump made it very clear China should not receive any Nvidia chips above H100s,” he said, referring to an older generation of the company's advanced AI chips. Commerce “has the pen, and you will have to ask them about their internal processes.” Bessent's comments were an unusually public rebuke of the Commerce Department, which oversees U.S. government controls over exports of sensitive, high-tech goods. The comments come as Nvidia’s ties to Singapore-based Megaspeed International, which prominently touts the companies’ partnership on its website, play a prominent role in the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Huang allegedly had an affair with the CEO of Megaspeed, Alice Huang, who U.S. intelligence suspects is a Chinese spy, the New York Times has reported. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has come under increasing scrutiny because of his reportedly close relationship with Huang. The Times reported Thursday that Lutnick resisted placing greater limits on the sale of Nvidia's more advanced chips to China. Chinese firms have accessed Nvidia's chips through companies like Megaspeed, which has purchased more than $4 billion worth of Nvidia's advanced semiconductors. The split in President Donald Trump's cabinet reflects the widespread fallout from the scandal that has engulfed Nvidia, one of the most valuable publicly-traded companies in the world. Nvidia's computer chips play a central role in the buildout of artificial intelligence, powering AI models such as those developed by Open AI and Anthropic. The U.S. government has, since the Biden administration, sought to restrict the sale of the most advanced AI computer chips to China in an effort to protect U.S. technology companies' lead. Yet China has at times retaliated, creating controversy over how far the U.S. should push its restrictions. The Commerce Department did not immediately respond to messages seeking comment. Bessent declined to comment Friday on the Times report that he confronted Lutnick last week in the White House's situation room. Separately, Axios reported this week that Lutnick received a classified memo this spring warning about Jensen Huang's relationship with a suspected spy. Numerous members of Congress have said they will investigate Lutnick's actions and called for him to testify on Capitol Hill. Richard Neal, both Democrats, wrote Lutnick a letter demanding that he preserve all records related to decisions about Nvidia chip exports, pending an investigation. Trump's approval of advanced Nvidia chip exports to China “raises critical questions about whether and to what extent political considerations are improperly influencing policy decisions made by the Administration,” Wyden and Neal wrote. John Kennedy of Louisiana, a member of the Senate Banking Committee, said he has questions for the commerce secretary and urged him to hold a press conference to explain what he knew. “The Commerce Department greenlit $4 billion of sales of advanced chips to the company of the spy that Mr. Huang was having an affair with and I want to know why," Kennedy said. "I want to know why the Commerce Department did it in light of the export controls, and everything I read indicates that this was a decision by the secretary himself." Kennedy added that Lutnick should testify before the Senate and should be subpoenaed if necessary. Huang resigned Thursday after news that he had an affair with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who U.S. intelligence suspects to be a Chinese spy, according to The Times. Last year, Megaspeed was accused of illicitly shipping advanced Nvidia computer chips into China, but in December said there was “no evidence” of such exports. On Thursday, Megaspeed maintained it takes its obligation to comply with American export control laws “extremely seriously” — and that it was committed to working “constructively and transparently” with the U.S. government.

AP-Yonhap WASHINGTON — Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Friday he was frustrated with the Commerce Department’s delay in implementing restrictions over the export of certain Nvidia chips to China. Bessent said on CNBC that his department, along with the departments of State and Defense and the U.S. Trade Representative, were in favor of adding Megaspeed to an export control list for months but that the Commerce Department was in charge of the matter. “I am frustrated when President Trump made it very clear China should not receive any Nvidia chips above H100s,” he said, referring to an older generation of the company's advanced AI chips. Commerce “has the pen, and you will have to ask them about their internal processes.” Bessent's comments were an unusually public rebuke of the Commerce Department, which oversees U.S. government controls over exports of sensitive, high-tech goods. The comments come as Nvidia’s ties to Singapore-based Megaspeed International, which prominently touts the companies’ partnership on its website, play a prominent role in the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Huang allegedly had an affair with the CEO of Megaspeed, Alice Huang, who U.S. intelligence suspects is a Chinese spy, the New York Times has reported. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has come under increasing scrutiny because of his reportedly close relationship with Huang. The Times reported Thursday that Lutnick resisted placing greater limits on the sale of Nvidia's more advanced chips to China. Chinese firms have accessed Nvidia's chips through companies like Megaspeed, which has purchased more than $4 billion worth of Nvidia's advanced semiconductors. The split in President Donald Trump's cabinet reflects the widespread fallout from the scandal that has engulfed Nvidia, one of the most valuable publicly-traded companies in the world. Nvidia's computer chips play a central role in the buildout of artificial intelligence, powering AI models such as those developed by Open AI and Anthropic. The U.S. government has, since the Biden administration, sought to restrict the sale of the most advanced AI computer chips to China in an effort to protect U.S. technology companies' lead. Yet China has at times retaliated, creating controversy over how far the U.S. should push its restrictions. The Commerce Department did not immediately respond to messages seeking comment. Bessent declined to comment Friday on the Times report that he confronted Lutnick last week in the White House's situation room. Separately, Axios reported this week that Lutnick received a classified memo this spring warning about Jensen Huang's relationship with a suspected spy. Numerous members of Congress have said they will investigate Lutnick's actions and called for him to testify on Capitol Hill. Richard Neal, both Democrats, wrote Lutnick a letter demanding that he preserve all records related to decisions about Nvidia chip exports, pending an investigation. Trump's approval of advanced Nvidia chip exports to China “raises critical questions about whether and to what extent political considerations are improperly influencing policy decisions made by the Administration,” Wyden and Neal wrote. John Kennedy of Louisiana, a member of the Senate Banking Committee, said he has questions for the commerce secretary and urged him to hold a press conference to explain what he knew. “The Commerce Department greenlit $4 billion of sales of advanced chips to the company of the spy that Mr. Huang was having an affair with and I want to know why," Kennedy said. "I want to know why the Commerce Department did it in light of the export controls, and everything I read indicates that this was a decision by the secretary himself." Kennedy added that Lutnick should testify before the Senate and should be subpoenaed if necessary. Huang resigned Thursday after news that he had an affair with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who U.S. intelligence suspects to be a Chinese spy, according to The Times. Last year, Megaspeed was accused of illicitly shipping advanced Nvidia computer chips into China, but in December said there was “no evidence” of such exports. On Thursday, Megaspeed maintained it takes its obligation to comply with American export control laws “extremely seriously” — and that it was committed to working “constructively and transparently” with the U.S. government.

Kennedy is pressing for a Senate committee to question Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent under oath about alleged Chinese access to restricted Nvidia chips, but he announced no hearing or enforcement action.

The alleged transactions put the effectiveness of those restrictions at the center of Kennedy’s questions.

And if secretary Lutnick is giving our chips away, he needs to stop it, in my opinion.

"In terms of cryptocurrencies, generally, I can say with almost certainty that they will come to a bad ending ," Buffett told CNBC in January.
"When it happens or how or anything else, I don't know."

For example, "If you buy something [like] a farm, an apartment house or an interest in a business and look to the asset itself to determine whether you've done something — what the farm produces, what the business earns ... it's a perfectly satisfactory investment," Buffett explains to Yahoo Finance .
"[I]f you ban trading in ... bitcoin, which nobody knows exactly what it is, people would say, 'Well why in the world would I buy it?'"
Still, many other investing experts like CNBC's Jim Cramer, Kevin O'Leary and Tony Robbins , also call buying cryptocurrencies a gamble.
They suggest thinking of it like rolling the dice in Las Vegas.

That's because it lacks intrinsic value, Buffett says. "If you buy something like bitcoin or some cryptocurrency, you don't have anything that is producing anything," Buffett says in an interview with Yahoo Finance . "You're just hoping the next guy pays more. And you only feel you'll find the next guy to pay more if he thinks he's going to find someone that's going to pay more. "You aren't investing when you do that, you're speculating." Famous for his " buy and hold " investment strategy, the Berkshire Hathaway CEO built his company — and his $82.8 billion net worth — backing companies that have substantive value. "Put together a portfolio of companies whose aggregate earnings march upward over the years, and so also will the portfolio's market value," Buffett wrote in his 1996 letter to shareholders. "If you aren't willing to own a stock for ten years, don't even think about owning it for ten minutes." To be an investment, what you're buying has to be worth something on its own, Buffett says. For example, "If you buy something [like] a farm, an apartment house or an interest in a business and look to the asset itself to determine whether you've done something — what the farm produces, what the business earns ... it's a perfectly satisfactory investment," Buffett explains to Yahoo Finance . "You look at the investment itself to deliver the return to you. "If you ban trading in farms, you could still buy farms, and have a perfectly decent investment," Buffett says. Bitcoin, however, only increases in value by being bought and sold, he argues. Its value comes from what people are willing to pay. "[I]f you ban trading in ... bitcoin, which nobody knows exactly what it is, people would say, 'Well why in the world would I buy it?'" The Oracle of Omaha has held this opinion since at least 2014, when he told CNBC of cryptocurrencies , "It's a mirage basically." "The idea that it has some huge intrinsic value is just a joke in my view," Buffett said. In 2017, bitcoin soared from below $1,000 at the start of the year to over $19,000 in December , catching the attention of everyone from J.P. Morgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon to NFL players. Tuesday, bitcoin traded near $8,900 according to CoinDesk's price index . Buffett sees a bleak future for the digital currency. "In terms of cryptocurrencies, generally, I can say with almost certainty that they will come to a bad ending ," Buffett told CNBC in January. "When it happens or how or anything else, I don't know." "I did not think [founder Jeff Bezos] could succeed on the scale he has," Buffett said to shareholders in May 2017. "There's nothing wrong with it if you want to gamble [that] somebody else will come along and pay you more money tomorrow," Buffett tells Yahoo Finance. "That's one kind of game. passages: For most of the past decade, Wall Street has often treated Warren Buffett's criticism of Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) as the old guard's final word on cryptocurrency.
Whether Buffett was right about Bitcoin largely depends on when the clock starts.
Buffett has been correct about Bitcoin's volatility.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Since Buffett's 2022 comment, Bitcoin reached its all-time high of $126,080, but it trades 51.8% below that peak.
Buffett's 2018 "rat poison squared" jab aged badly on price: Bitcoin has surged 522% since, while Berkshire Class B shares gained 189%.
Berkshire has beaten Bitcoin since Buffett said he wouldn't pay $25 for all the world's Bitcoin, gaining 79% versus 61%.
Despite this growth, Bitcoin's latest decline has strengthened Buffett's supporters.
Berkshire, now headed by CEO Greg Abel with Buffett as chairman, has never directly invested in Bitcoin.
If Bitcoin continues to decline and falls below its summer low of $57,700, Buffett's $25 remark may appear even more accurate over time.
Some market analysts link the November selloff to the debut of a major AI listing, a connection tested in a look at whether the Anthropic IPO is why Bitcoin is crashing.

"When it happens or how or anything else, I don't know."

For example, "If you buy something [like] a farm, an apartment house or an interest in a business and look to the asset itself to determine whether you've done something — what the farm produces, what the business earns ... it's a perfectly satisfactory investment," Buffett explains to Yahoo Finance .

extraction.body: When it comes to bitcoin, billionaire investor Warren Buffett wants to make one thing clear: Unlike buying stocks, bonds or real estate, buying bitcoin is not an investment. That's because it lacks intrinsic value, Buffett says. "If you buy something like bitcoin or some cryptocurrency, you don't have anything that is producing anything," Buffett says in an interview with Yahoo Finance . "You're just hoping the next guy pays more. And you only feel you'll find the next guy to pay more if he thinks he's going to find someone that's going to pay more. "You aren't investing when you do that, you're speculating." Famous for his " buy and hold " investment strategy, the Berkshire Hathaway CEO built his company — and his $82.8 billion net worth — backing companies that have substantive value. "Put together a portfolio of companies whose aggregate earnings march upward over the years, and so also will the portfolio's market value," Buffett wrote in his 1996 letter to shareholders. "If you aren't willing to own a stock for ten years, don't even think about owning it for ten minutes." To be an investment, what you're buying has to be worth something on its own, Buffett says. For example, "If you buy something [like] a farm, an apartment house or an interest in a business and look to the asset itself to determine whether you've done something — what the farm produces, what the business earns ... it's a perfectly satisfactory investment," Buffett explains to Yahoo Finance . "You look at the investment itself to deliver the return to you. "If you ban trading in farms, you could still buy farms, and have a perfectly decent investment," Buffett says. Bitcoin, however, only increases in value by being bought and sold, he argues. Its value comes from what people are willing to pay. "[I]f you ban trading in ... bitcoin, which nobody knows exactly what it is, people would say, 'Well why in the world would I buy it?'" The Oracle of Omaha has held this opinion since at least 2014, when he told CNBC of cryptocurrencies , "It's a mirage basically." "The idea that it has some huge intrinsic value is just a joke in my view," Buffett said. In 2017, bitcoin soared from below $1,000 at the start of the year to over $19,000 in December , catching the attention of everyone from J.P. Morgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon to NFL players. Tuesday, bitcoin traded near $8,900 according to CoinDesk's price index . Buffett sees a bleak future for the digital currency. "In terms of cryptocurrencies, generally, I can say with almost certainty that they will come to a bad ending ," Buffett told CNBC in January. "When it happens or how or anything else, I don't know." Of course, Buffett has been wrong about backing new technologies before. He missed opportunities to invest in Google and Amazon, decisions he now calls mistakes . "I did not think [founder Jeff Bezos] could succeed on the scale he has," Buffett said to shareholders in May 2017. Crypto-enthusiasts argue that Buffet doesn't understand blockchain-based coins, and he has admitted as much. Still, many other investing experts like CNBC's Jim Cramer, Kevin O'Leary and Tony Robbins , also call buying cryptocurrencies a gamble. They suggest thinking of it like rolling the dice in Las Vegas. "As long as you can afford to lose everything you put into it, go with it," O'Leary told CNBC Make It in December, 2017 . "There's nothing wrong with it if you want to gamble [that] somebody else will come along and pay you more money tomorrow," Buffett tells Yahoo Finance. "That's one kind of game. That is not investing." Don't miss: Here's how much grad school cost when Warren Buffett graduated in 1951, compared to today Like this story? Like CNBC Make It on Facebook ! facts.text: When it comes to bitcoin, billionaire investor Warren Buffett wants to make one thing clear: Unlike buying stocks, bonds or real estate, buying bitcoin is not an investment.
Don't miss: Here's how much grad school cost when Warren Buffett graduated in 1951, compared to today
"In terms of cryptocurrencies, generally, I can say with almost certainty that they will come to a bad ending ," Buffett told CNBC in January.
"When it happens or how or anything else, I don't know."

For example, "If you buy something [like] a farm, an apartment house or an interest in a business and look to the asset itself to determine whether you've done something — what the farm produces, what the business earns ... it's a perfectly satisfactory investment," Buffett explains to Yahoo Finance .
"[I]f you ban trading in ... bitcoin, which nobody knows exactly what it is, people would say, 'Well why in the world would I buy it?'"
Still, many other investing experts like CNBC's Jim Cramer, Kevin O'Leary and Tony Robbins , also call buying cryptocurrencies a gamble.
They suggest thinking of it like rolling the dice in Las Vegas.

Sam Daodu is a crypto analyst and the editor of 24/7 Wall St.'s Crypto Desk, where he covers Bitcoin, XRP, Ethereum, Solana and the altcoins investors search for most.
His work focuses on price levels, spot ETF flows, on-chain data and the regulatory decisions that move crypto markets, written so a first-time buyer and a seasoned trader can both use it.
Sam has written about crypto professionally since 2019 and has published more than 2,000 articles.
His analysis is syndicated on Yahoo Finance, MSN and AOL and has been cited by other crypto news sites.
He also founded MacLabs Marketing, a content and personal branding agency for crypto founders and executives.
When he isn't reading charts, Sam is usually at the gym or watching One Piece, a series he maintains has better tokenomics than most altcoins.
Buffett has been correct about Bitcoin’s volatility.
On pricing, Buffett’s 2018 remark hasn’t aged well.
Since May 7, 2018, the first trading day following his comment, Berkshire’s Class B shares have gained 189.3%.
That’s a solid return, but it lags far behind Bitcoin’s 522.4% increase, from $9,769 to $60,801.
Since Buffett’s 2022 comment, Bitcoin reached its all-time high of $126,080, but it trades 51.8% below that peak.
Despite this growth, Bitcoin’s latest decline has strengthened Buffett’s supporters.

One of Buffett’s most famous statements came during Berkshire Hathaway’s annual meeting weekend on May 5, 2018, when he told an interviewer that Bitcoin is “probably rat poison squared.” On that day, Bitcoin closed at $9,769.
This means that an investor who shared Buffett’s view and chose Berkshire over Bitcoin has seen better returns.
Berkshire, now headed by CEO Greg Abel with Buffett as chairman, has never directly invested in Bitcoin.
If Bitcoin continues to decline and falls below its summer low of $57,700, Buffett’s $25 remark may appear even more accurate over time.
Some market analysts link the November selloff to the debut of a major AI listing, a connection tested in a look at whether the Anthropic IPO is why Bitcoin is crashing .
Chainlink has been outpacing Bitcoin in the recent crypto rebound, but a shorter road to recovery and billions in institutional demand may make one coin a far more compelling buy right now.

contextFacts.text: Still, many other investing experts like CNBC's Jim Cramer, Kevin O'Leary and Tony Robbins , also call buying cryptocurrencies a gamble.
They suggest thinking of it like rolling the dice in Las Vegas.

passages: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent declined on Sunday, Nov.
22, to endorse a return by Jensen Huang to the top job at Nvidia , saying investigators first need to establish who was responsible for any chip sales that broke US export rules.
"I think we have to see where the buck stops," Bessent said on CBS's "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" when asked whether it would be a good idea for Huang to go back and run the company [1] .
Bessent also said the administration has not received the answers he demanded from Nvidia a week ago.
"We've been in touch with the temporary management, with the lead directors, with their lawyers, and we do need answers" [1] .

On Megaspeed, the Singapore company Alice Huang ran, Bessent said investigators "will see if Megaspeed was indeed a pass-through company, a front company based in Singapore, to get the high-end chips to Chinese entities." He said Nvidia removed Megaspeed from its sales list in August 2025 and that Treasury and other departments have pushed for it to be blacklisted, but called last week's remote-access rule, which stops certain countries and entities from using chips through leased capacity, possibly "more important" [1] .
Huang has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee and will also be interviewed by House panels in early December, CBS News reported [2] .
MLQ.ai has covered his agreement to testify publicly and California's subpoena of Nvidia , which the state attorney general says covers potential criminal violations.

"I think that is kind of a canard," he said, framing the issue as whether Nvidia had a culture of compliance "versus the one person's foibles." Pressed that she was allegedly a Chinese spy, he said: "I assume he didn't know that she was an alleged spy" [1] .

Asked about House Foreign Affairs Committee documents showing Commerce approved sales of more than 800,000 Nvidia and AMD AI chips to China, including to companies linked to the Chinese military, Bessent said the president had drawn a hard line at the H200 and that the buyers were "companies that do business with the Chinese military," not the military itself.
On Friday he told CNBC that no further curbs on older Nvidia chips are needed .
He said he had confidence that Nvidia's board committees "are moving very quickly on this and will come up with some very fulsome and robust answers" [1] .
Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been running the company since Huang resigned, CBS News noted [2] .
He added that the people to examine include whoever ran compliance, "normally, it's the legal department, the general counsel's office" [1] .
Brennan put it to Bessent that President Trump has said Huang should get his job back while Bessent had urged the board to look outside the company for a new chief executive.
Trump said Huang deserved a second chance earlier this week.

On Nvidia's role in AI financing, Bessent called it "one of our great companies" and said that, with the CFO in charge, "I believe that she understands the financing quite well," adding that there is "near unlimited demand for their chips worldwide" [1] .

extraction.body: Bessent also withheld support for Jensen Huang's return as CEO, saying investigations should conclude before a leader is chosen. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Sunday that Nvidia has yet to explain how its AI chips reached China, and he withheld support for Jensen Huang's return as CEO. The United States is investigating whether Nvidia gave China access to advanced AI chips despite government restrictions, CBS News reported. On Nov. 15, Bessent gave Nvidia 10 days to answer questions about its compliance with export rules in an interview with Fox News. Seven days into that period, Bessent appeared on CBS's "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" and said the administration still lacked the answers it sought. "We don't, Margaret," he said. Officials have contacted Nvidia's interim management, lead directors and lawyers, Bessent said. "It behooves Nvidia to move quickly on this because we want to know what the culture was," he said. "We do need to see who was in charge of compliance there," Bessent said. He also asked, "Was it at the lower levels? Was it at the middle levels? Did it go all the way to the top?". During his Nov. 15 Fox News interview, Bessent raised the possibility of a "culture of noncompliance" at Nvidia and asked whether it was "pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings." He said Sunday that such a culture was only a possibility. "We will see, and that's why I think the board is moving very quickly to establish whether this did or did not exist," he said. Asked about Nvidia's reported "handshake" business approach, Bessent said, "For deals that size, there's no such thing as an untraceable handshake deal." The shipments of chips left financial and documentary trails, he said. "They may not be the 100-page documents, but it will be possible to understand what has gone on here," he said. Bessent said he had confidence that Nvidia's internal committees "will come up with some very fulsome and robust answers." Bessent said the investigations should conclude before Nvidia's next leader is decided. Asked about Huang's return, he said, "I think we have to see where the buck stops," and asked, "Were these malicious actors down at the bottom of the company who were responsible for the noncompliance?". President Donald Trump took a different position at a news conference Friday, saying he wanted Huang to return as chief executive. "I think the company, if they were smart, they'd take that brilliant man, accept an apology and let him go back to work," Trump said earlier. Huang resigned following reports of extramarital affairs, one involving Alice Huang, an alleged spy according to CBS News. The New York Times reported that Huang stepped down after acknowledging an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence had identified as a Chinese asset. Bessent called the affair "kind of a canard" and said company culture mattered more than one person's foibles. "I assume that he didn't know that she was an alleged spy," he said. The Justice and Commerce Departments said last week that they were pursuing a criminal investigation into Megaspeed, a Singapore company Alice Huang once led. Officials are examining whether Megaspeed smuggled Nvidia chips into China, while the Securities and Exchange Commission, or SEC, is investigating Nvidia's accounting practices, according to the Times. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has led Nvidia since Huang's departure. Bessent said last week that he thought Nvidia's leadership needed a major shake-up. He has urged the company to appoint an outsider to run it. It was not immediately known whether Nvidia will deliver the answers before Bessent's 10-day window closes. Huang is scheduled to testify at a private House hearing on Dec. 1; he is also expected to appear before the Senate Banking Committee.

coreStoryFacts.text: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent declined on Sunday, Nov.
22, to endorse a return by Jensen Huang to the top job at Nvidia , saying investigators first need to establish who was responsible for any chip sales that broke US export rules.
"I think we have to see where the buck stops," Bessent said on CBS's "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" when asked whether it would be a good idea for Huang to go back and run the company [1] .
Bessent also said the administration has not received the answers he demanded from Nvidia a week ago.
"We've been in touch with the temporary management, with the lead directors, with their lawyers, and we do need answers" [1] .

On Megaspeed, the Singapore company Alice Huang ran, Bessent said investigators "will see if Megaspeed was indeed a pass-through company, a front company based in Singapore, to get the high-end chips to Chinese entities." He said Nvidia removed Megaspeed from its sales list in August 2025 and that Treasury and other departments have pushed for it to be blacklisted, but called last week's remote-access rule, which stops certain countries and entities from using chips through leased capacity, possibly "more important" [1] .
Huang has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee and will also be interviewed by House panels in early December, CBS News reported [2] .
MLQ.ai has covered his agreement to testify publicly and California's subpoena of Nvidia , which the state attorney general says covers potential criminal violations.

"I think that is kind of a canard," he said, framing the issue as whether Nvidia had a culture of compliance "versus the one person's foibles." Pressed that she was allegedly a Chinese spy, he said: "I assume he didn't know that she was an alleged spy" [1] .

Asked about House Foreign Affairs Committee documents showing Commerce approved sales of more than 800,000 Nvidia and AMD AI chips to China, including to companies linked to the Chinese military, Bessent said the president had drawn a hard line at the H200 and that the buyers were "companies that do business with the Chinese military," not the military itself.
On Friday he told CNBC that no further curbs on older Nvidia chips are needed .
He said he had confidence that Nvidia's board committees "are moving very quickly on this and will come up with some very fulsome and robust answers" [1] .
Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been running the company since Huang resigned, CBS News noted [2] .
He added that the people to examine include whoever ran compliance, "normally, it's the legal department, the general counsel's office" [1] .
Brennan put it to Bessent that President Trump has said Huang should get his job back while Bessent had urged the board to look outside the company for a new chief executive.
Trump said Huang deserved a second chance earlier this week.

On Nvidia's role in AI financing, Bessent called it "one of our great companies" and said that, with the CFO in charge, "I believe that she understands the financing quite well," adding that there is "near unlimited demand for their chips worldwide" [1] .
